824c97d0ff07c5e9: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The government is examining measures to address the sale of uncertified imported products via e-commerce platforms, including potential action against platforms that fail to ensure compliance with quality standards.

Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said his ministry will collaborate with the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to ensure that products sold online meet established standards.

“Many products brought in from abroad are delivered as individual parcels. Although sold at low prices, these items lack quality certification, this includes electrical goods, which are required to meet safety standards.

“So, I have held discussions with KPDN and relevant parties to explore ways to regulate the operations of e-commerce platforms, while simultaneously continuing to encourage the public to purchase goods online,” he told reporters after the Majlis SIRIM Industry 2026 here yesterday.

Johari said this initiative is crucial for protecting consumers from poor-quality or hazardous products, and for ensuring that local manufacturers, who bear the costs of certification, do not face unfair competition from cheaper imported products.

Meanwhile, in his speech, Johari said products entering the Malaysian market must comply with both Malaysian and international standards, just as domestically produced goods are required to meet stringent regulatory requirements.
“In this respect, Malaysia remains firmly committed to addressing the importation and sale of non-compliant products in our domestic market.
“These products not only expose Malaysian consumers to potentially serious health and safety risks but also undermines the competitiveness of our domestic industries,” he said.

The Majlis SIRIM Industri 2026 witnessed SIRIM QAS International Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of SIRIM Bhd, becoming the first certification body in Malaysia and Southeast Asia to receive accreditation for the AS9110 Quality Management System Requirements for Aviation Maintenance Organisations.

AS9110 is an internationally recognised standard for aviation maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) organisations, addressing critical areas such as airworthiness and fight safety, maintenance planning and execution, inspection and testing, risk management, human factors, traceability and technical data control. — Bernama
44cedc05b3bca4c4: KUALA LUMPUR: Nasyid group Brothers is planning to release a new album, despite acknowledging that their music may not draw the same attention it once did after a long break from the industry.
Member Yasin Sulaiman, 51, said the group's passion for making music and keeping the legacy of nasyid alive remains as strong as ever.
He added that the upcoming album is simply about sharing their music with fans, even as the industry and audience tastes have evolved.
"There's no denying that times have changed and this is no longer our era. What matters is that we do it because we love it.
"Whether there are listeners or not, we will continue. If people listen, that's a bonus. We do what we enjoy," he said.
Yasin, alongside fellow members Abdullah Faiz Mohamad and Syah Rizal Mohamed, spoke at a press conference here yesterday for the upcoming Malaysian Nasyid Legends concert.
He noted that while recording has yet to begin, the new album will revisit familiar themes from Brothers' earlier work, such as humanity, friendship and life's struggles.
"We have discussed the album, but it has not been recorded yet," he said.
Yasin added that the concert will mark Brothers' first time performing together on stage in more than seven years, giving them a valuable chance to introduce themselves to a younger crowd.

"People know the song Teman Sejati, but they don't know us. Perhaps our appearance at this concert will help people discover who Brothers are. We want to share our music with the new generation," he said.

Scheduled for May 27, 2027, at the Setia City Convention Centre in Shah Alam, the Malaysian Nasyid Legends concert will feature nine acts—bringing together veterans Raihan, Rabbani, Hijjaz, Inteam, Saujana, UNIC and Nowseeheart, alongside newer group Aeydan.
d518f318c37e0e79: KUALA LUMPUR: Referee Hanna Hattab was replaced at half-time in Wednesday's AFC Champions League Two match in Abu Dhabi between Al Jazira and Gol Gohar amid serious accusations of alleged drunkenness.
Gol Gohar, the Iranian side facing Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates, saw Hattab make several questionable decisions. One in the 32nd minute stood out.
After a foul on Gol Gohar player Ali Asghar Ashouri in midfield, Hattab paused before making his decision.
The Syrian referee then called over Al Jazira goalkeeper Ersin Destanoglu and showed him a yellow card, to everyone's surprise.
The Turkish goalkeeper and his team-mates looked baffled by Hattab's decision. The referee did not look particularly alert.
Footage shows Gol Gohar coach Mehdi Rahmati shouting, "He's drunk!" after the incident.
The accusations remain unconfirmed, but the AFC intervened at half-time.
Gol Gohar team manager Heydar Afsari said after the match: "The referee against Al Jazira was not in a normal state, and even Al Jazira's players told us the same thing."
"The club immediately informed the match officials and warned that we would not play if the situation remained the same."
"Al Jazira's number 77 (Joao Milson) should have been sent off after his second foul, but the referee instead recorded the card under the opposing goalkeeper's name."
"The referee was replaced after we informed the AFC," Afsari said.
Al Jazira won 1-0 thanks to a goal from Anderson Talisca.
53f61e6acd4da2c4: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A government review has so far found no strong evidence that Malaysian-linked plantation companies were responsible for fires in Indonesia, the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) has said.

In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, the ministry said it had worked with the Plantation and Commodities Ministry to examine allegations linking Malaysian companies to the fires through their ownership, investments or operations in Indonesia.
“Based on the review to date, there is no strong evidence confirming the involvement of Malaysian-linked plantation companies as the parties responsible for the fires,” it said.
The government has yet to commit to introducing legislation to hold individuals and companies accountable for overseas operations that contribute to transboundary haze affecting Malaysia.

The ministry said it had examined the merits of introducing a transboundary haze pollution act on several occasions, taking into account enforcement challenges, diplomatic relations and the experience of other countries with similar legislation.

“The effectiveness of a law depends not only on the existence of its provisions, but also on the ability to obtain evidence, conduct investigations and enforce the law against parties outside Malaysia’s jurisdiction,” it said.

Establishing responsibility for fires overseas would require sufficient data, including land ownership records and information about companies operating at fire sites, raising issues of confidentiality, security and national sovereignty.

The ministry pointed to the Second Asean Haze-Free Roadmap (2023–2030), which encourages member states to adopt policies such as the “polluter pays” principle to hold those responsible for pollution accountable under their respective domestic laws.
“Enforcement action against any party responsible for fires is subject to the jurisdiction and domestic laws of the Asean member state where the fires and haze originate,” it said.
The ministry said the immediate priority was to strengthen domestic enforcement against open burning across Asean, improve information sharing and deepen cross-border enforcement cooperation.

The reply was in response to Bakri Member of Parliament Tan Hong Pin (PH-DAP), who had asked whether the government would reconsider introducing legislation to hold Malaysian individuals and companies accountable for transboundary haze caused by their overseas operations.
The ministry did not disclose how many companies had been examined, identify them or provide a timeline for a decision on the proposed legislation.
716c3bd1b357a078: KUCHING, Nov 26 — The introduction of 11 new faces in Gabungan Parti Sarawak’s (GPS) candidate line-up for the 13th Sarawak State Election reflects the coalition’s efforts to rejuvenate its leadership and encourage greater participation of young professionals in politics.

GPS information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the inclusion of younger candidates, particularly from Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), was a positive development towards ensuring leadership continuity within the coalition.

“Most of the new faces are from PBB. What makes me even more pleased is that almost all of them are relatively young, in their 40s. Most of them are also professionals, which is a positive development.

“Therefore, we hope that these new faces will win the election as part of our efforts to rejuvenate the party and, at the same time, bring the younger generation into leadership,” he told reporters after officiating the BorneoCraft Global 2.0 Expo and Conference (BCG 2.0) here, yesterday.
GPS yesterday announced its full line-up of 82 candidates for the Dec 12 state election, with new faces accounting for approximately 13.4 per cent of the candidates.

Meanwhile, commenting on the recent resignation of senior leaders from GPS component parties, Abdul Karim said such developments should serve as an opportunity for political parties to evaluate their internal weaknesses and strengthen their organisational maturity.
“My personal view is that it could probably make the party more mature. When you see veteran party members leaving, it should prompt the party to reflect on what is happening internally,” he said.

Abdul Karim said disagreements and dissatisfaction with leadership were not uncommon in party politics but declined to elaborate on internal matters involving the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), a GPS component party.

Earlier, five PDP service committees in Paradom, Sungai Bidut, Engkilo, Sungai Sadit and Sungai Empawah announced their collective withdrawal from the party following the resignation of former Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) president Datuk Seri Wong Soon Koh from PDP.
The Election Commission (EC) has fixed Saturday (Nov 28) for nomination, Dec 8 for early voting and Dec 12 for polling.
For the latest news on the state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/sarawak/2026/. — Bernama

23947d9f45ad65a3: JAKARTA: Rescuers will resume the search on Thursday for 13 workers trapped underground in an illegal gold mine in Indonesia's West Java province, with 13 already confirmed dead, police and rescue authorities said.
In the Bogor region, south of the capital Jakarta, a total of 26 workers entered the mine on Monday when heavy rains inundated the shaft, leaving them trapped 100 metres underground.
Hengki, West Java's police chief, told Reuters that six of the 13 fatalities had been identified. The search would continue on Thursday, barring bad weather conditions, he added.
Access to the mine has been made more difficult by the narrow, slippery and dark conditions of the shaft, authorities said.
Indonesia's search and rescue agency said rescuers were focusing on two mine shafts and using ropes to gain access, but the 100-metre depth of the excavation complicated search efforts.
Small-scale and illegal mining have caused a series of accidents in Indonesia, where mineral resources are located in remote areas under conditions that are difficult for authorities to regulate.
In January, several miners were killed by carbon monoxide poisoning at an illegal gold mine in the same area, local news outlet Detik reported.
State miner Antam, which runs gold mining operations in the region, said the incident occurred at an unauthorised mine and was not part of its operations.
61770676cd05c4a3: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A fatal road incident in Johor is now being investigated as murder after police uncovered a suspected cable theft link following the discovery of a video circulating on Facebook.
One man died and another was seriously injured in the incident involving a car and a motorcycle in Taman Nusa Bestari, Iskandar Puteri in Johor.
Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said in a statement that police received a report of the incident at 4.30am on Tuesday.
The two local men, aged 22 and 34, sustained severe head and leg injuries and were taken to hospital, where one of them died at 10am yesterday. The deceased was not identified in the statement.
The case was initially investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
However, police subsequently discovered a video of the incident circulating on Facebook, posted by a user under the handle “Azman Mann Terr”.
“Further investigation found elements of cable theft behind the incident,” Radin Ramlan said, adding that Telekom Malaysia Johor Baru had also lodged a police report.
The case is now being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, Section 431A of the same law and Section 235 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Police have not disclosed how the suspected cable theft was connected to the incident.
“We are now tracking the suspects and call upon witnesses or those who have information on the incident to come forward to assist the police with investigation,” Radin Ramlan said.
Anyone with information is urged to contact the Iskandar Puteri police control centre at 07-511 3622 or its hotline at 07-511 4486.

1d227140baa5ebec: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday as investors remained cautious over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, driving demand for safer assets.
At 8 am, the local currency strengthened to 4.1135/1220 against the greenback compared with yesterday’s close of 4.1170/1220.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar index (DXY) fell 0.10 per cent to 103.708 points, despite an increase in the United States’ Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation rate to 3.8 per cent in October from 3.7 per cent in September.
He said the two-year and 10-year US Treasury yields also fell by four and seven basis points to 4.65 per cent and 4.86 per cent, respectively.
“The decline in US Treasury yields gives the impression that there was a flight-to-quality as markets were having doubts whether the AI boom will continue to support AI-related stock prices.
“As such, ringgit is expected to maintain its tight range trade today,” he told Bernama.
At the opening, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.

It eased against the euro to 4.5125/5218 from 4.5036/5091 at Wednesday’s close, edged down vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.3932/4044 from 5.3756/3821, and was softer against the Japanese yen to 2.5837/5892 from 2.5820/5853.
Against its Asean peers, the ringgit traded mixed.

It inched up vis-a-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 224.4/224.9 from 224.6/224, but depreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.1880/1951 from 3.1858/1899 and lower against the Thai baht to 12.0751/1093 from 12.0599/0798.
The local note was flat versus the Philippine peso at 6.46/6.48. — Bernama
ee55757b48209cce: ALOR STAR: A woman has appealed for help to locate her younger brother, a Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) student who has been missing for nearly five weeks.
Nur Fatihah Mat Daud, 33, of Kampung Sedaka Tengah, Yan, said she only learnt of her brother Muhammad Shafik Hidayat's disappearance three days ago through a WhatsApp message that went viral.
She said she was informed that her 22-year-old brother had not attended classes at the university for some time, and that UKM had contacted her for information about his whereabouts.
"The last time I was in touch with him was on Oct 3, when I sent him to board a bus to Kajang.
"He was still responding to my messages as usual then, but he stopped replying whenever I tried to contact him after that," she said.
She said her brother had never mentioned having any problems, and she had assumed he was attending classes as usual.
Nur Fatihah said the two were the only siblings and had lost their parents four to five years ago.
"After our parents died, he is all I have. I sincerely hope he will be found safe.

"I have lodged a police report, and the university has also informed me that it has filed one. I urge anyone with information or who has seen him to come forward or contact the nearest police station," she said.
The disappearance of the third-year student from UKM's Faculty of Science and Technology went viral on social media, with reports that he had been absent from classes for nearly five weeks.
The university said it had tried contacting him by phone but received no response. It urged anyone with information about his whereabouts to contact the university or police.
9b925581e0faf580: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia recorded 56,802 online scam cases involving losses of RM1.56 billion in the first 10 months of 2026, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told the Dewan Rakyat on Nov 25.
In a separate parliamentary update, the deputy communications minister said more than 724,000 pieces of online gambling-related content were taken down between January 2025 and October 2026.
The figure highlights the scale of content removed, but does not show how widely it had circulated before being taken down.
Removing harmful material can limit its spread. However, by the time a scam advertisement is reported, many people may already have seen it. This highlights the need for earlier intervention.
One measure platforms can take is to screen paid advertisements before they go live.
For example, when reviewing an investment advertisement, a platform can check who paid for it, where its link leads and whether it resembles advertisements previously removed for fraud.
Publishing separate figures for suspected scam advertisements blocked before publication and those removed afterwards would give users a clearer picture of how effective these checks are.
What users see also depends on the content recommended by platforms.
This is particularly important for children, who may come across betting promotions disguised as ordinary videos.
Parents can help children recognise such promotions. Platforms, meanwhile, can adjust recommendations for younger users and give families greater control over who can contact them.
Early intervention also requires platforms to consider context.
A warning about a fake investment scheme, for instance, may include a screenshot of the scam itself.
If such a warning is restricted, platforms should provide a clear explanation and an avenue for users to request a review. This would help prevent legitimate warnings from being mistakenly removed.
Ultimately, online safety is a shared responsibility.
Users can flag suspicious material, regulators can enforce the rules, and platforms can make responsible decisions about the content they promote.
The effectiveness of these responsibilities is best reflected in the decisions made before anyone has reason to complain.

1bbd079e75c326a9: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has withdrawn his final bid to revive a RM1.9 million lawsuit against former attorney general Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, ending a six-year legal battle over Thomas’ decision to prosecute him.

Najib withdrew his application for leave to appeal to the Federal Court today, with his lawyer, Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin, telling the court that his client wanted to “focus on pressing issues”, Free Malaysia Todayreported.
A three-member Federal Court bench chaired by Justice Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah struck out the application after lawyers for both sides confirmed an agreement for Najib to pay RM10,000 in costs.
Najib was present in court, where family members and supporters filled the public gallery.

The former prime minister launched the legal action in 2020, accusing Thomas of misfeasance in public office, malicious process and negligence in exercising his constitutional powers to prosecute in cases involving 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and the International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC).
He sought RM1.9 million in special damages to cover the cost of hiring an audit team to examine documents and assist in preparing his defence.
The High Court struck out the lawsuit in November 2022, a decision upheld by the Court of Appeal on January 13 this year.
Najib subsequently sought permission in March to take the case to the Federal Court, putting forward three questions of law for its consideration.
In its January ruling, the Court of Appeal found that Najib’s lawsuit had been filed prematurely, as the criminal proceedings in question had yet to begin when he initiated the civil action.
It also held that the tort of malicious process was not recognised under Malaysian law.
However, the appellate court rejected the High Court’s findings that Thomas enjoyed immunity and that his actions were beyond judicial scrutiny.
c4e3fad7a8f2f161: PUTRAJAYA: Datuk Seri Najib Razak has withdrawn his application to reinstate a RM1.9 million civil suit against former attorney-general (A-G) Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, saying he wants to focus on more pressing matters.

Najib's lawyer, Datuk Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin, informed a Federal Court bench led by Chief Justice of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah that the former prime minister had decided not to pursue the application.
"The applicant has decided to focus on more pressing issues and wishes to withdraw the application," he said.
Firoz said Thomas' legal team had agreed to costs of RM10,000.
Thomas' lawyer, Alan Adrian Gomez, confirmed the agreement.
Hashim then struck out the application and ordered Najib to pay RM10,000 in costs to Thomas.
Also sitting on the bench were Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and Datuk Azimah Omar.
Najib, 73, arrived at the courtroom at 8.55am, dressed in a black suit and red tie.
The appearance marked his first court attendance since returning home to Jalan Langgak Duta from Kajang Prison on Nov 10, following the granting of house arrest.
He appeared in good spirits, smiling and greeting supporters seated in the public gallery.
While waiting for proceedings to begin, he was seen browsing a book.
Thomas was not present in court.
Among those present was former Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Irwan Serigar Abdullah.
Firoz was accompanied by Yudistra Darma Dorai, while Gomez appeared with Mervyn Lai.

Najib filed the suit against Thomas on Oct 22, 2021, alleging that the latter had abused his powers by initiating criminal proceedings against him in connection with the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) scandal.
Najib claimed that Thomas had acted maliciously in bringing charges against him involving 1MDB and the International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC).
Among other reliefs, Najib sought a declaration that Thomas had committed misfeasance in public office, as well as RM1.9 million in special damages.
The amount included expenses incurred in engaging an audit team to examine documents and prepare his defence in the criminal proceedings.
Thomas served as A-G from June 4, 2018, to Feb 28, 2020.
On Nov 25, 2022, the Kuala Lumpur High Court allowed Thomas' application to strike out Najib's suit without a full trial.
Najib subsequently appealed against the decision, but a three-member Court of Appeal bench dismissed his appeal on Jan 13 this year.
The appellate court agreed with the High Court that the suit was premature, as the criminal proceedings against Najib had yet to commence when the civil action was filed.
On Feb 10, Najib filed a notice of motion seeking to challenge the appellate court's decision, raising three questions of law for the Federal Court's determination.
He also sought permission to file a notice of appeal within a month if leave was granted.

dc103c8a1f222668: HONG KONG: Hongkongers laid flowers on Thursday at the site of a horrific fire that ripped through seven apartment blocks and killed 168 people a year ago, but authorities in the Chinese territory have warned against "acts of disorder".

The world's deadliest residential building blaze since 1980 began on the afternoon of Nov 26, 2025, at Wang Fuk Court and raged for two days, with orange flames and black smoke visible for miles around.
A year on, authorities appear wary of commemorations taking on a political tone and have planned no official memorial, but some religious establishments have organised events.
On Wednesday evening, sobs were heard as hundreds of people attended an emotional memorial service at a Hong Kong church, with four people who lost relatives reading out the names of the victims.
"I can no longer be with them. It's a searing pain in my heart, and I suffer from insomnia every night," said Jenny Lam, a pastor who lost three family members.
"They are not just a number, each one of them was a unique life," said Reverend Dominic Chan, presiding over the service at the Catholic Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception.
The blaze was Hong Kong's worst disaster in more than seven decades, and a shock to the 7.5 million residents of one of Asia's safest cities.
'CHAOS' AND 'DISORDER'
On the anniversary on Thursday, some Catholic and Buddhist places of worship were also set to host events to pray for the dead.
By late Wednesday, dozens of people had laid flowers in a small authorised space near the fire site, and others followed suit on Thursday morning, in the shadow of the charred buildings.
The city's number two official, Eric Chan, said the government would offer help to "lawful" events, while warning against "acts of disorder".

The Chinese government's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office warned this week against attempts to "cause chaos" under the guise of remembering the disaster, telling residents to remain vigilant against "individuals with ulterior motives who might stir up trouble".
Human Rights Watch said the Hong Kong government was "using Beijing's tactics of shutting out the voices of the victims and promising an elusive accountability".

John Burns, a politics professor at the University of Hong Kong, told AFP that the space for public anger and criticism was "much narrower" than before Beijing imposed a national security law in 2020, following huge and sometimes violent pro-democracy protests.
'PERFECT STORM'
A report last month from a judge-led inquiry said the fire was likely started by a cigarette and spread quickly via netting on building facades.
Authorities admitted that the tragedy was a "perfect storm" exposing longstanding flaws in regulation and a slack enforcement attitude.
Police told AFP that 40 people had been arrested in connection with the blaze.
Last month, Hong Kong leader John Lee led some of his ministers in bowing in apology, and the housing chief resigned.
Still, public administration scholar Sonny Lo said that bottom-up pressure for accountability was lacking because of "weak" civil society, media and legislature.

In a letter to journalists on Wednesday, Beijing's top diplomat in Hong Kong admitted that the fire exposed "weak links" in building maintenance and fire safety regulation, adding that investigations and reform were underway.

feaaa2b30803f04a: TAWAU: Most public services in the district continue to operate as usual despite a power disruption affecting Sabah's east coast since this morning.
Checks at several government premises and banking institutions found that essential services remained unaffected, thanks to the use of generator sets as an alternative power supply.
At Tawau Hospital, routine services continued as usual with support from high-capacity generators.
Emergency services, including the use of operating theatres for emergency cases, were also unaffected, while measures to conserve electricity were implemented throughout the disruption.
Checks at the Tawau Federal Building, which houses state and federal government departments and agencies, also found that operations were running as usual with the help of existing generators.
The same was observed at the Tawau Municipal Council office, where services continued to operate normally.
However, some routine transactions, including online bill payments, were disrupted as the system went offline.
Banking services were generally unaffected by the use of generators, although some automated teller machines (ATMs) reportedly experienced disruptions.
In the business sector, checks found that several restaurants had to operate in darkness, while others used generators to continue their operations.
Earlier, Sabah Electricity said the power disruption, which began at 6.04am, was caused by an incident involving the electricity transmission system.
The government-linked company said its operations room had been activated, while technical teams were working to restore power in Sandakan, Tawau and Lahad Datu in stages.
The actual cause of the incident was still being investigated, and further updates would be provided as they became available.
fa7eaed2c336876f: SINGAPORE, Nov 26 — When coffee is spilled at an office block in a futuristic enclave of Singapore, AI-powered cameras and sensors detect it and send a cleaning robot right away.
The wheeled robot receives a signal from an operations hub, rolls off its dock and takes a lift to the eighth floor, where it finds the mess and clears it up – all without human intervention.
It was part of a staged demonstration in Punggol Digital District in suburban Singapore, where the city-state is carrying out real-world trials of tech that could become part of everyday life.

A district-wide “live test-bed” of this kind, allowing companies to experiment in an urban environment, is rare globally, said Tang Bing Wan, chief digital and technology officer at JTC Corporation, Singapore’s industrial landlord.

The government-developed mini-city, PDD for short, spans 50 hectares (120 acres) – a bit bigger than Vatican City – and currently houses eight businesses and office blocks, as well as a mall, university campus and metro station.
“Companies that dabble in robotics, cybersecurity and even the financial services industry” are based there, with more set to join, Tang told AFP.
PDD, which borders residential areas, is not strikingly futuristic to walk around.
But behind the scenes, a centralised digital platform helps run infrastructure, from waste disposal to elevators.
There are also plenty of robots around – including machines designed to alleviate the ageing city-state’s manpower crunch in areas such as cleaning and security.
A wheeled robot that can deliver food orders to offices is also being trialled.
Central platform
Despite the shrinking workforce, Singapore residents expect their surroundings to remain clean, safe and well-maintained, said Ong Chen Hui of the Infocomm Media Development Authority.
“Robotics offers a real part of the solution” by doing physically taxing routine tasks, freeing up workers for jobs requiring “human judgement, care, and skill”, Ong said.
The district will be formally inaugurated next month in a grand ceremony headed by the prime minister.

A district-wide “open digital platform” coordinates the robots and connects different locations, gathering data from thousands of cameras and sensors on everything from air temperature to foot traffic.
Artificial intelligence analyses the data, enabling the system – with the help of human operators – to respond to problems, anticipate disruption, and reduce energy use and waste.
Elevator movements can be reduced during periods of low demand, while restaurants can anticipate busy hours to adjust staffing and food preparation.
Centralised air-conditioning controls can also be adjusted in real time, to use less power.
A digital replica of the district displayed on a giant screen at the operations centre gives staff there a real-time view of PDD and helps them spot or predict anomalies.

PDD probably has “the highest concentration of robots in Singapore where they can roam freely, because the estate is designed” that way, said James Tan, a director at government technology arm GovTech.
‘Not dystopian’
Companies use PDD to test their robots and other new tech before wider deployment, and JTC’s Tang said safety rules are being crafted to prevent accidents.
“It’s not a dystopian future. That’s not what’s happening here,” he said.
Hospital worker Amanda Lim, 34, who lives nearby, said her children like the robots.
“They will chase and play with them,” she said while strolling with her family at the mall.
Despite increasing global concern over the potential risks of AI technology, no one AFP spoke to at PDD expressed concern over data privacy or surveillance.

Among the companies leading trials in the government-built district is homegrown LionsBot, which makes fleets of cleaning machines for what it envisions as the “cleaner of the future” who will no longer be holding a mop.
And Japan’s Panasonic is testing a shared communications system for robots from different manufacturers, using PDD’s digital infrastructure.
Takeshi Ando, managing director at Panasonic’s innovation centre at PDD, said similar trials conducted in Japan took more time.
Ando explained that, unlike at PDD, he had to deal individually with a fragmented group of building managers, regulators and government agencies.
The district’s university campus, the Singapore Institute of Technology, allows academics to “work very closely and almost seamlessly with companies”, said its president Chua Kee Chaing.
In the surrounding neighbourhood, too, autonomous shuttles – carrying a human safety operator – are already ferrying passengers on public roads.
Retiree Veronica Tan, 62, was unfazed by the increasing automation.

0f1f8f3312856150: KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has decided to take no further action (NFA) on the investigation into a letter sent by the former Malaysian External Intelligence Organisation (MEIO) director-general to the United States Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) ahead of the 14th General Election (GE14).
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the decision was made on Nov 25, 2025, after the A-GC reviewed investigation papers submitted by the police.
He said police investigated the matter under Precinct 7 police report 8959/23.

"The investigation was conducted under Section 8(1) of the Official Secrets Act 1972 (Act 88), Section 203A of the Penal Code (Act 574) and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588).
"Investigations found no instruction or authorisation from any government authority on the matter," he said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.

Pang Hok Liong (PH-Labis) had asked whether police found that the letter, which sought US support for the Najib administration ahead of GE14, was sent with the authorisation or instruction of any government authority, and the outcome of the investigation.
Saifuddin said the investigation papers were referred to the A-GC on Dec 18, 2023, for review and further instructions.
The A-GC decided on NFA on Nov 25, 2025, after reviewing the investigation findings, he added.

In July 2018, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak said he had never instructed MEIO, which operated under the Research Division of the Prime Minister's Department, to write the letter seeking CIA support ahead of the May 9 general election.
The three-page letter, dated May 4, 2018, was signed by then MEIO director-general Hasanah Abdul Hamid and addressed to then CIA director-designate Gina Haspel.
It requested continued US support for the Najib administration if Barisan Nasional won GE14 by a narrow margin or secured only a single-seat majority.
3760fc368104265d: PUTRAJAYA: Former prime minister Najib Razak has withdrawn his final bid to revive his RM1.9 million lawsuit against former attorney-general Tommy Thomas, abandoning his application for leave to appeal to the Federal Court.
His lawyer, Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin, told a three-member bench in Putrajaya today that the former prime minister was withdrawing the application to "focus on pressing issues".
Firoz said Thomas's lawyers had agreed to accept RM10,000 in costs. Thomas's counsel, Alan Adrian Gomez, confirmed this.
Justice Hashim Hamzah, who chaired the bench comprising Justices Ruzima Ghazali and Azimah Omar, subsequently struck out the application.
Najib was in court, and the public gallery was filled with family members and supporters.
Najib filed the leave application in March to challenge the Court of Appeal ruling upholding the dismissal of his suit. He had framed three questions of law for the Federal Court.
On Jan 13, a Court of Appeal panel of Justices P Ravinthran, Wong Kian Kheong and Nadzarin Wok Nordin dismissed his appeal and affirmed the High Court's Nov 25, 2022 decision to strike out the suit.

Najib filed the lawsuit against Thomas in 2020 for alleged misfeasance in public office, malicious process and negligence in the exercise of prosecutorial discretion under Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution in relation to 1MDB and the International Petroleum Investment Company charges.
He sought RM1.9 million in special damages for the cost of engaging an audit team to review documents and help prepare his defence.

Delivering the Court of Appeal's decision, Ravinthran, who has been elevated to the Federal Court, said the panel agreed with the High Court that the action was premature because the criminal cases had not begun when the suit was filed.
He said the tort of malicious process was not recognised under Malaysian law.
The Court of Appeal, however, disagreed with the High Court's findings that Thomas enjoyed immunity and that his actions were non-justiciable.
32034e18a1ef6d27: ACTRESS Nabila Huda believes staying active across all platforms is key to keeping her acting sharp, urging fellow performers not to be too precious about their status.
The 41-year-old star said turning down jobs to hold out for big-screen roles or streaming shows is unrealistic in a crowded industry.

"For me, whatever offers come along, we have to take them. We shouldn't be too fussy about maintaining our status as an actor. For example, wanting to act only in films or only on over-the-top (OTT) platforms. That won't do."
She pointed out that film roles are scarce when so many actors are competing for work, adding, "Whether the role is small or big, if I get an offer and it's a suitable script, I'll do it."
For Nabila, steady work is like daily practice for a musician, stopping her skills from getting rusty.
"I won't stop (acting) because indirectly, that's how we polish our acting talent. It's just like singing; if we can't sing for a year, it doesn't work," she said.
Recalling a three-month break from the set, she admitted that returning to work left her feeling stiff and out of rhythm.
"Whether we like it or not, we really have to act, even if it's just a small cameo. Otherwise, that skill will be lost."
Open to any platform, she is now keen on fresh scripts and roles she has never tried before.
With more than 20 years in the industry, Nabila credits her steady stream of work to caring for her mother, treating people well, and being easy to work with.

"On the outside, I might seem troublesome. But for me, I believe that when we mind our manners with the people we've worked with, mind our politeness and respect others, people won't get tired of calling us and will feel comfortable working with us," she said.
Growing up around film sets gave her a close bond with cast and crew alike, whom she sees as family.
She also stressed that she acts out of genuine love for the job rather than chasing fame or trophies.

"As an actor, I don't have any mission to become popular, to be on top or to win awards," she said, adding that she still sees herself as a learner who remembers her tough early days and stays humble.

The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Jonathan Lim Hsi How, while the man was represented by lawyers Boston Ho and Clement Hii. — The Borneo Post

2002c36141d193ce: NEW YORK: US consumers grappling with high consumer prices have been "increasingly selective" in discretionary purchases, according to a Federal Reserve report released Wednesday describing economic conditions around the country.
The Fed's latest "Beige Book" pointed to weakening in auto sales and residential real estate activity but characterized tourism and travel as "solid" and hospitality overall as "mixed."
Higher energy prices acted as a drag on auto sales, while lofty diesel prices were flagged as a problem in five districts.
Of the 12 districts, eight reported "slight to moderate" growth while four reported no change.

Surging lending rates contributed to lackluster real estate activity. The rate on the 30-year fixed US mortgage remains 7.2 percent, up almost a point from the year-ago period, according to the latest data from mortgage finance giant Freddie Mac.
"Contacts across a range of sectors reported sustained cost pressure from energy, transportation, healthcare, insurance, and tariff-related expense," the report said.

"Input cost growth generally outpaced increases in selling prices, as competitive pressures and customer price sensitivity limited firms' ability to fully pass through higher costs," it continued. "Contacts expected both expenses and prices to continue rising in the coming months."
On the positive side, the report said employment levels "rose slightly," with contacts in several sectors citing "steady or rising labor demand."

Companies reported persistent difficulties filling skilled and technical roles. That dynamic was also a source of upward pressure on wages, along with increases in costs for health insurance and other benefits.
The Fed's next monetary policy meeting will be December 8-9.
Futures markets overwhelmingly expect the central bank to lift interest rates by one-quarter point from the current level of 3.75-4.00 percent.

61953facbe684332: SYDNEY: Australian business investment surged anew in the September quarter as firms poured money into data centres, recording its biggest rise since 2011 at the height of the mining boom, while companies further upgraded spending plans for coming months.

The strong numbers on Thursday suggested some resilience in the Australian economy even as five interest rate hikes this year triggered the biggest housing downturn in 40 years, hit consumer spending and weakened the labour market. The local dollar rose 0.2 per cent to US$0.6640, and three-year government bond futures reversed earlier gains to be down three ticks to 95.51.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported private capital spending jumped 12.2 per cent in the third quarter to an inflation-adjusted A$59.5 billion ($39.37 billion), far above market forecasts of a 4.4 per cent rise.

That was led by an 87 per cent jump in spending on information media and telecommunications equipment amid record investment in server racks and processing gear for data centres. Much of this was on imported equipment and thus an offsetting drag on economic growth.

Abhijit Surya, senior APAC economist at Capital Economics, said spending on information and communications technology could nearly double in the 2027 financial year, in contrast with the rest of the economy, where capital spending was struggling to tread water.
"With the RBA clearly concerned about capacity pressures, the data suggest it won't be in a rush to cut rates anytime soon," Surya said.

Markets are still wagering that the next move in interest rates will be down but do not fully price a first cut from the Reserve Bank of Australia until August. A June cut is now seen as an 83 per cent chance.

Overall spending on plant and machinery shot up 23.1 per cent, while spending on buildings and structures rose 1.7 per cent. An ABS survey of firms showed they planned to spend A$223.7 billion in the year to June 2027, 11.8 per cent higher than the previous estimate.

7194f3a9184f12c3: KUALA LUMPUR: Seizures at the nation's entry points by the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) surged nearly fourfold to RM322.74 million up to October, from RM82.10 million in its first year of operation in 2025.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the seizures involved 16,357 enforcement cases, with the biosecurity sector accounting for RM72.05 million and customs and taxation RM50.84 million.

Among the major seizures were those at Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas (RM21.37 million), Penang Port (RM7.14 million) and the Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex (RM3.62 million).
"The effectiveness of MCBA's integrated controls and inspections is evident from the significant increase in enforcement performance.

"Its achievements show that the agency is not merely an administrative restructuring, but a high-impact institutional reform that strengthens border security, facilitates trade and tourism, and protects national revenue," he said in a written reply to Rodziah Ismail (PH-Ampang) in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
MCBA was established following a cabinet decision on Jan 3, 2024, under the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency Act 2024 (Act 860), which came into force on Jan 1, 2025.

It began pilot operations at the Rantau Panjang ICQS on Jan 1, 2025, before expanding to 21 major entry points the following month. It now oversees 123 active land, air and sea entry points nationwide.

The agency integrates the inspection and enforcement functions of six agencies — the Immigration Department, Customs Department, Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department, Health Ministry, Road Transport Department and Wildlife and National Parks Department — under a single chain of command.

The merger was completed with the implementation of the Border Control and Protection Service Scheme on July 1, 2026, through appointment transfer options for existing personnel and the recruitment of 408 officers.

The new intake comprises 39 assistant superintendents and 369 assistant enforcement officers assigned to the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link entry points at Bukit Chagar in Johor Baru and Woodlands North in Singapore.

Saifuddin said passenger and cargo screening had also been strengthened through technology integration, including the Advance Passenger Screening System (APSS), mandatory Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) submissions and stricter checks on travel documents and accommodation bookings.
Officers and supervisors have also been deployed at e-Gate lanes to strengthen monitoring.
The Johor Baru-Singapore RTS Link at the Sultan Ibrahim Complex in Bukit Chagar will pioneer a co-located international entry point model, with operations expected to begin by February 2027.

Separately, a 100 per cent screening operation at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), involving Aviation Security (Avsec), the police , Customs and Perhilitan, was conducted from Aug 10 to Nov 13.
The operation screened 4,569 flights and 21,526 flight crew, while 483,119 pat-downs were conducted and 711,160 checked bags inspected across 10 major destinations.
It detected 16 prohibited items and foiled 16 drug smuggling attempts involving 436.66kg of drugs worth RM34.89 million.

On integrity breaches involving counter-setting and flying passport syndicates, Saifuddin said action had been taken against 27 officers up to November, with 19 dismissed and eight suspended pending court charges.
8ea9b1d2f0c6849f: NEW YORK, Nov 26 — S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia’s “AA” credit rating on watch for a potential downgrade on Wednesday, warning that the abrupt resignation and swift reinstatement of chief executive Jensen Huang revealed systemic deficiencies in management and board oversight at the world’s premier artificial intelligence chipmaker.

“We believe the long tenure of certain board ‌members may have compromised their independence. The company’s corporate governance practices may also not have kept pace with Nvidia’s rapid growth and its role as a critical global technology enabler,” the ratings agency said.

According to Reuters, S&P indicated it could downgrade Nvidia by one notch within the next 90 days, cautioning that a more severe cut could follow if continuing regulatory investigations inflict lasting damage on the company’s corporate reputation or commercial prospects.

The credit warning compounds an unprecedented period of executive instability in Silicon Valley. Nvidia directors reinstated Huang on Monday, barely a week after the 63-year-old co-founder resigned over revelations of extramarital relationships with direct reports and a former executive at Singapore-based cloud provider Megaspeed.

The reversal drew intense criticism from corporate governance specialists and lawmakers, particularly after the board’s newly appointed chair had assured institutional investors that Huang would not return because his personal conduct breached the company’s code of conduct.

In announcing his return, Nvidia omitted reference to the workplace misconduct, stating instead that the decision was “based on US government input,” while an independent board committee continued probing reports surrounding foreign intelligence efforts.

The political pressure surrounding the reinstatement was underscored by reports that the US Department of Justice conducted no formal inquiry into Huang before President Donald Trump publicly lobbied for his return.

Federal authorities reportedly concluded there was no evidence he violated federal statutes based on existing export-smuggling investigations into client firms Super Micro and Megaspeed International, though prosecutors cautioned that the assessment remains fluid.

Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that a classified congressional briefing by the CIA, FBI, National Security Agency, and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence found no indication that Beijing directed tech executive Alice Huang to target Jensen Huang.

While intelligence officers noted that Alice Huang maintained contact with China’s Ministry of State Security during the relationship and that her husband, Kang Wei, was an active intelligence asset, officials assessed that the affair was romantic rather than an orchestrated state intelligence operation.

Rival agency Moody’s struck a more pragmatic tone, affirming Nvidia’s Aa1 rating with a stable outlook. Moody’s argued that returning Huang to the helm eliminates critical leadership transition risks and stabilizes core operational execution, even as regulatory and board governance uncertainties persist.

Equity markets took S&P’s warning in stride, with Nvidia shares sliding nearly four per cent on Wednesday to extend a broader 38 per cent decline since early October, while debt insurance costs held steady.

The governance upheaval arrives as analysts scrutinise Nvidia’s circular financing arrangements across the technology sector. By aggressively bankrolling artificial intelligence startups, specialized cloud operators, and data centre developments that subsequently reinvest those capital injections into Nvidia’s proprietary computing hardware, the semiconductor giant faces heightened vulnerability to systemic shocks if broader industry spending cools.
186cb86d6998c2ec: WASHINGTON: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade on Wednesday, saying the departure and subsequent reinstatement of its chief executive officer (CEO) had exposed weaknesses in the chipmaker's management and board oversight.

The company's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang earlier this week, days after he resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs with his direct reports as well as a Chinese businesswoman alleged by US intelligence to be Beijing's spy.

Critics and lawmakers slammed the reinstatement, questioning the independence of the board, whose newly elected chair had told investors last week Nvidia would not rehire Huang as CEO because his personal behaviour was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct.

Reinstating Huang on Monday, Nvidia omitted any mention of his affairs, saying instead the move was "based on US government input", even as an independent board committee continued its investigation into reports involving him and a suspected foreign intelligence effort.

Instead, it concluded that there was no evidence he had broken any laws based on ongoing investigations into two Nvidia clients, Super Micro and Megaspeed International, which are suspected of smuggling advanced microchips to China. That determination is subject to change as the probes continue.
NO EVIDENCE YET THAT ALICE HUANG IS A SPY

Investors were largely unruffled by the S&P move, which comes with Nvidia shares down 38% since October 6. Nvidia closed down nearly 4.0 per cent on Wednesday, retracing some declines after the Nasdaq 100 index briefly flirted with a 20 per cent decline from its recent high.
The cost of insurance against tech companies defaulting on debts has jumped sharply in recent weeks, but the five-year CDS spread for Nvidia was little changed.
Nvidia currently has an 'AA' rating from S&P, which indicates a very strong capacity to meet financial commitments. The highest rating is 'AAA'.

The agency said it could downgrade Nvidia within the next 90 days but expects any potential downgrade to be limited to one notch, unless investigations and other disclosures harm the company's reputation or future business prospects.

Meanwhile, Moody's said on Wednesday that bringing back Huang eases near-term uncertainty around Nvidia's business execution and eliminates execution risk associated with appointing a new leader for the chipmaker.
The agency said Nvidia's Aa1 rating and stable outlook remain unaffected but added that governance and regulatory uncertainty persist.
Nvidia has played a key role in financing the AI boom, bankrolling AI startups, cloud firms and data centre projects, which in turn spend much of that capital on Nvidia's own GPUs and other AI chips.
The complex financing arrangements have increased Nvidia's exposure to a potential downturn, analysts said.

Separately, the Wall Street Journal on Wednesday reported that US officials found no evidence that tech executive Alice Huang was directed by Beijing to spy on Jensen Huang, citing people familiar with a classified briefing.

Officials from the CIA, FBI, Office of the Director of National Intelligence and National Security Agency briefed staff from congressional intelligence committees and chamber leaders, the Journal reported.
The officials said Alice Huang contacted China's spy agency during the affair but found no indication that she provided significant intelligence, the Journal reported.
Nvidia and the agencies did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

The report said current evidence suggests Alice Huang and Jensen Huang may have had an amorous relationship, but it was not a coordinated play by China, and that new information could change that assessment.

The briefing also noted that Kang Wei, described to the Journal as Alice Huang's husband by people who know them, was an asset for China's Ministry of State Security who remained in frequent contact with the intelligence service.

dc48251483a483a0: NEW YORK, Nov 26 — New York has postponed the iconic Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday over fears of extreme weather, a first in the event’s 100-year history, as a major storm gathers steam on the US East Coast.
The brewing “nor’easter” threatens to disrupt plans for as many as 80 million people hitting the road and flying around the Thursday holiday, one of the country’s busiest travel seasons.

“The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” parade sponsor Macy’s wrote in a statement shared by City Hall.
“Due to the expected severe weather, the 100th March of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will move to Saturday, November 28.”
The annual parade sees brightly coloured balloons travel some 2.5 miles (four kilometres) from Midtown Manhattan to Macy’s Herald Square flagship store on 34th Street.
Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. It is the first time in its history that it has been postponed, The New York Post reported.

“This will be a heavy storm. We are expecting sustained winds between 30 and 40 miles per hour, with gusts as high as 60 to 65 miles per hour possible,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani told a safety briefing Wednesday.
“The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning as well as a coastal flood warning.
“Winds will be strong enough (Thursday) to down tree limbs and power lines.” Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade in 1997.
Volunteers struggled but failed to keep a tight rein on ropes which constantly threatened to slam into onlookers.
The careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” – from the popular children’s book – toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious.
Another balloon, the purple dinosaur known to children as “Barney,” went out of control prompting police armed with scissors to puncture and deflate the balloon.
Yet another casualty was the “Pink Panther” balloon, which blew up over 42nd Street, sending shreds of pink rubber confetti raining on bystanders.

“While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants – and spectators – is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss. — AFP

4d7510a105797812: Terlebih dahulu, saya perlu memberitahu bahawa 'Tan Sri' dan 'Dato Seri' pada tajuk penulisan ini ialah anugerah kebesaran yang dipakai Presiden PAS Hadi Awang. Artikel ini sekadar menjelaskan apa yang dinyatakan beliau tempoh hari adalah salah.
Saya petik laporan FMT kelmarin. Kata Hadi partinya semakin mendapat sokongan golongan bukan Islam, namun golongan yang beliau maksudkan ialah mereka yang dia sifatkan sebagai 'tidak ekstrem'.
Jadi adakah Hadi menyifatkan semua orang bukan Islam yang tidak menyokong PAS golongan 'ekstrem'?

Apakah takrif 'ekstrem' menurut pandangan presiden PAS itu? Siapakah golongan 'tidak ekstrem' yang presiden PAS itu maksudkan? Saya kira MCA, MIC dan juga Gerakan, kerana Hadi pernah kata PAS boleh dan sudah bekerjasama dengan tiga parti itu.

Namun, penerimaan Hadi akan MCA dan MIC ialah berdasarkan dua parti itu komponen Barisan Nasional, dan PAS mempunyai persefahaman dengan BN sejak PRN Negeri Sembilan. Gerakan pula sememangnya komponen Perikatan Nasional. Maka, tidak bolehlah kita menyamakan sokongan tiga parti itu dengan sokongan masyarakat bukan Islam, kerana tiga parti itu tidak lagi mewakili komuniti itu secara menyeluruh.

Apa pun, menurut Hadi, PAS yakin mampu menewaskan PH pada PRU16 kelak berdasarkan 'keputusan memberangsangkan' dalam beberapa PRN baru-baru ini. Jelas beliau merujuk kepada PRN Johor, Negeri Sembilan dan Melaka.
Tetapi keputusan memberangsangkan di tiga PRN itu tercapai hasil kerjasama dengan Umno. Hakikatnya, gandingan PAS-Umno disokong pengundi Melayu, bukannya pengundi bukan Melayu bukan Islam.

Diakui Hadi banyak menyumbang kepada pencapaian bergaya itu apabila menyeru penyokong PAS mengundi BN. Kenyataan beliau bahawa wajib orang Islam sokong calon Islam diakui sebilangan besar pengundi Melayu. Bagaimanapun that same statement telah menyaksikan golongan bukan Islam bukan Melayu menjauhi PAS. Bukanlah rahsia mereka tidak senang dengan kenyataan Hadi, sedangkan ramai pemimpin bukan Melayu yang baik dan bersih. Bahkan, perasaan orang bukan Islam terguris apabila Hadi mendakwa orang bukan Islam sebagai punca gejala rasuah.
Jadi apabila Hadi kata PAS semakin dapat sokongan bukan Islam adalah sesuatu yang tidak betul.

Untuk double confirm pendapat saya itu, saya bertanya beberapa penyelidik yang membuat kaji selidik di lapangan semasa tiga PRN tempoh hari. Seorang daripada mereka memberitahu saya bahawa apa yang dikatakan Hadi itu tidak betul, menurut dapatan para penyelidik. Seorang lagi kata "finding saya: tak betul".
Ringkasnya, Hadi salah dalam rumusannya.

Kenyataan Hadi sememangnya pelik. Saya yang tidak berbekalkan hasil penyelidikan pun boleh rasa majoriti orang bukan lslam tidak sokong PAS, tidak kira 'ekstrem' atau 'tak ekstrem' (sekadar meminjam istilah Hadi).

Daripada mana Hadi dapat maklumat sehingga beliau boleh merumuskan sokongan bukan Islam kepada PAS semakin meningkat? Mustahil para penyelidik PAS tak tahu keadaan sebenar -- tak mungkin mereka tidak beri laporan tepat dan benar kepada presiden.
Adakah Hadi punya intel sendiri? Maklumlah presiden memang wajar ada banyak saluran maklumat tetapi apa yang beliau umumkan itu tidak betul.

Mungkinkah apa yang Hadi katakan itu bertujuan menyuntik semangat pemimpin dan ahli parti supaya mereka mempunyai keyakinan bagi menghadapi PRU kelak? Tetapi, bak dikata tadi, tentu mereka juga ada maklumat sendiri mengenai keadaan sebenar.
Atau mungkin Hadi sekadar main psywar untuk menakutkan pihak lawan, atau Hadi mahu menenangkan perasaan Umno yang mungkin gusar kenyataan Hadi akan membuatkan orang bukan Islam menjauhi PAS-Umno?
Mungkinkah juga untuk tenangkan perasaan ahli PAS sendiri yang memendam rasa tetapi risau kata-kata Hadi akan menyusahkan parti memikat hati pengundi bukan Islam?

Imbau kembali PRN Melaka. Tidak sampai 48 jam sebelum orang Melaka keluar mengundi, Hadi berucap di pentas grand finale BN-PN untuk memberi peringatan tentang pentingnya umat Islam keluar mengundi. OK, no problem with that.

Kata beliau, dalam Islam perkiraan politik dibuat berlandaskan faktor dosa dan pahala berbanding orang bukan Islam yang dituduhnya 'zalim'. Katanya lagi, kesan daripada orang Islam tidak keluar mengundi ialah 'orang lain' yang akan jadi pemerintah, dan menurut Hadi mereka akan bertindak mengikut perkiraan sendiri dan mengabaikan amanah yang diwajibkan Allah.
Siapakah 'orang lain' yang beliau maksudkan? Saya kira umum tahu.
Apapun beliau kata sebab itu orang Islam mesti tunaikan kewajipan mengundi untuk memimpin seluruh manusia. Do you think orang bukan Islam senang dengan kata-kata itu?
Apa lagi ini: "sejahat-jahat orang Islam seburuk-buruk orang Islam memerintah negeri, mereka tidak sezalim orang bukan Islam." Tuduhan ini memang menyakiti hati orang bukan Islam.

Menurut Malaysiakini, setiausaha politik kepada Hadi iaitu Syahir Sulaiman memberitahu portal berita itu bahawa kenyataan Hadi kononnya merujuk kepada apa yang berlaku dalam sejarah pemerintahan Islam.
Bagi saya, penjelasan itu sukar diterima kerana maksud dan sasaran Hadi memang jelas. Ia mencetuskan kemarahan orang bukan Islam termasuk parti yang mengaku sekutu PAS.

Menyusuli kenyataan Pejabat Presiden PAS yang mendakwa kata-kata Hadi dipetik di luar konteks, ini pada hemat saya tidak lebih daripada usaha damage control. Hakikatnya apa yang Hadi kata tidak boleh atau susah dipertahankan. Apatah lagi ada video ucapan.
Realitinya Hadi did say what he said. Soal luar konteks tidak timbul. Pejabat Presiden PAS pun tidak menafikan, cuma mendakwa kenyataan Hadi was taken out of context.

Mungkin Hadi mahu buktikan kepada semua pihak termasuk ahli parti bahawa kenyataannya tidak mendatangkan mudarat -- sebaliknya PAS semakin dapat sokongan orang bukan Islam meskipun facts and figures showed otherwise.
Kesimpulan terbaik dibuat seorang penganalisis politik, apabila berkata: "Kalau Hadi yang kata, yang pelik-pelik ni tak menghairankan."
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
f58b3b59193abc2b: MANUFACTURING is entering a new phase as artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and automation reshape production processes, prompting companies to rethink their operations and workforce development strategies.

For manufacturers, the shift goes beyond introducing more machines. It involves integrating technology into production processes, improving operational efficiency and equipping employees with the skills needed to work alongside increasingly sophisticated systems.

These developments were among the key issues discussed at FOZ One's recent "Innovation Meets Industry" dialogue, which brought together robotics experts, academics and industry representatives to examine emerging technologies and their potential applications in manufacturing.

The dialogue provided a platform for participants to exchange views on industrial innovation, robotics and the changing demands of modern manufacturing, while exploring how technological advancements could be translated into practical business and industrial applications.
Among those attending was Professor Zexiang Li, co-founder of DJI and Googol Technology, founder of XbotPark and tenured professor at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST).
Also present were members of QKM Technology's senior leadership team, representatives from local universities, industry associations and the automation sector.

Academic participants included Multimedia University (MMU) Professor Ir Ts Dr Jerry Ng Poh Kiat, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) Department of Control and Mechatronics Engineering representative Ts Dr Mohd Najeb Jamaludin, and University of Southampton Malaysia assistant professor and electrical and electronic engineering lecturer Ir Dr Ahmad Syahrin Idris.
Southern University College Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology dean Chan Bun Sheng also attended.

Industry representatives included Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) branch chairman Saw Seong Ho, Malaysian Plastics Manufacturers Association (MPMA) Johor branch chairman Mike Tan, Johor Bahru Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (JBCCI) president Dato' Jeffrey, and DF Automation & Robotics director Dr Yeong Che Fai.
Moving towards smarter manufacturing
The discussions highlighted how technologies such as AI, robotics and automation could help manufacturers improve production processes, enhance precision and make better use of operational data.
As industries continue to embrace these advancements, demand for skilled workers capable of using emerging technologies is also growing.
MMU Professor Ir Ts Dr Jerry Ng Poh Kiat highlighted the importance of robotics education in preparing the next generation of engineers for this transition.

He said rapid technological advancements and industrial transformation were reshaping workforce requirements, with greater emphasis on productivity, resilience and innovation amid intensifying global competition.
Developing engineers who can integrate different technologies and apply their knowledge to solve real-world problems would therefore be crucial in bridging the gap between education and industry.

From the industry perspective, QKM Technology co-founder and chairman Dr. Jinbo Shi shared how AI, robotics and automation were transforming manufacturing operations, particularly by improving productivity, product quality and operational efficiency.
Automation, for instance, allows machines to perform repetitive tasks, potentially reducing manual workloads and improving consistency.
Robotics can support more complex and precision-based operations, while AI can analyse production data to identify patterns, detect potential problems and support operational decision-making.
When integrated with digital systems, these technologies can also improve coordination across different stages of production, giving manufacturers greater visibility over their operations.
However, adopting technology is not simply a matter of purchasing new equipment.
Shi highlighted the importance of applying technological solutions to address actual manufacturing challenges, ensuring that innovation translates into meaningful improvements on the factory floor.

Manufacturers must consider how new systems can be integrated into existing production lines, whether employees have the necessary skills to operate them and whether investments can deliver measurable improvements.

For FOZ One, the dialogue forms part of its efforts to explore opportunities to enhance its manufacturing capabilities as a global original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and original design manufacturer (ODM).
The transition towards smarter manufacturing could create opportunities to improve productivity, strengthen quality control and respond more effectively to changing customer requirements.
People remain central to automation
The growing use of robotics and automation has also raised questions about the future role of workers in manufacturing.

While machines can take over repetitive and labour-intensive processes, people remain essential in managing production systems, monitoring performance, resolving problems and ensuring quality standards are maintained.
The transition therefore requires manufacturers to prioritise workforce development alongside technology adoption.
During the dialogue, QKM Technology chief human resources officer Wang Hong highlighted the importance of preparing young talent for the evolving demands of the manufacturing industry.

The discussion emphasised how universities and companies could work together to provide students with practical training, exposure to real industry projects and hands-on experience, helping them develop the technical knowledge and skills required in modern manufacturing.
For FOZ One, equipping existing employees with the knowledge and skills needed to adapt to changing manufacturing processes is also an important part of this transition.
As production systems become more sophisticated, workers may need to develop capabilities in operating automated equipment, understanding digital systems and working alongside industrial robots.

Training and reskilling are therefore important considerations for companies seeking to introduce new technologies while retaining the experience and operational knowledge of their existing workforce.

Rather than viewing automation solely as a means of reducing labour requirements, manufacturers have an opportunity to reorganise tasks and allow employees to focus on responsibilities requiring human judgement, technical expertise and problem-solving skills.
Building for the next phase

The wider adoption of AI, robotics and automation is expected to influence how manufacturers compete, particularly as customers increasingly demand greater efficiency, consistent product quality and shorter production cycles.
For companies such as FOZ One, keeping pace with these developments involves understanding which technologies are relevant to their operations and how they can be applied effectively.
Beyond manufacturing technology, the dialogue also explored how innovation could be translated into successful businesses.

Li shared his experience in nurturing technology-driven businesses, highlighting the role of practical education, hands-on learning and strong industry support in turning innovative ideas into commercial opportunities.

Drawing on examples such as DJI and Googol Technology, he emphasised the importance of encouraging creativity and developing problem-solving skills, while providing aspiring entrepreneurs with the support needed to bring their ideas to market.

He also highlighted the value of closer collaboration between universities and industry, enabling students and researchers to gain practical exposure, identify real-world challenges and develop solutions with commercial potential.

The exchange among academics, technology specialists and industry representatives also highlighted the importance of collaboration in translating technological developments into practical industrial applications.
Universities and research institutions can contribute technical expertise, while industry players provide insights into operational requirements and commercial challenges.
Such partnerships could help bridge the gap between research and industrial adoption, creating opportunities for manufacturers to explore new solutions and strengthen their capabilities.

The discussions also offered insights into how Malaysia could further develop its smart manufacturing capabilities, encourage technology entrepreneurship and nurture a skilled workforce for the future.
For FOZ One, its engagement with the technology and manufacturing ecosystem reflects its efforts to explore how innovation can support its long-term business development.
As the manufacturing landscape evolves, the ability to combine technology, industry expertise and workforce capabilities will remain crucial.
The challenge is not simply to introduce more machines, but to build manufacturing operations in which people, robotics and AI work together to deliver better outcomes.
