cc28ab398e3752f0: SYDNEY: Asian shares eked out a rare rally on Thursday after Wall Street fought back from deep lows, though concerns over the circular financing of AI and a new round of US tariffs made for a muted mood in a holiday-thinned session.
Tech giant Nvidia was again at the centre of the unease after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade citing weaknesses in the chipmaker's management and board oversight.
Nvidia stock ended down 3.9% at US$149.30 on Wednesday, US$2.3 trillion short of its October peak of US$243.37.
Wall Street did recoup most of its initial losses overnight as money moved into other, more defensive, sectors. S&P 500 futures added 0.5% early on Thursday, while Nasdaq futures firmed 0.4%.
Japan's Nikkei gained 1.6% and South Korea's main index rose 1.9%. Japan is down 8% for the month, while South Korea has shed 16% and Taiwan 15%.
Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan edged up 0.6%, but were still off 9% for November so far.
Bond investors are wondering if the broad losses in stocks coupled with doubts on the durability of AI-driven business investment might temper the hawkishness of central banks.

It was notable that Treasury yields hit multi-week lows on Wednesday even as US economic growth for the third quarter was revised up sharply to 4.3%, while the Federal Reserve's favoured measure of core inflation hit an uncomfortably high 3.3%.
While futures still imply a 98% chance the Fed will raise rates by 25 basis points in December, speculation of a half-point increase has faded.
Yields on 10-year paper were off at 4.848%, having touched an 11-week trough overnight.
Tariffs add to inflation risk

Still, the outlook for inflation was not helped by White House proposals for new tariffs on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union, though crucially the new duties will not stack on top of those imposed in July.

"The latest US tariff announcement is not as alarming as it looks, and the increase in the effective tariff rate looks set to be a touch lower than we've been assuming," said Stephen Brown, chief North America economist at Capital Economics.
"The additional tariff burden is likely to be small, but will still provide a marginal boost to prices and keep core goods inflation firm into next year."
In currency markets, the dollar's recent strength was tempered somewhat by the drop in Treasury yields, with the dollar index easing a touch to 103.71.
The safe-haven Swiss franc was a major gainer as the dollar slipped to 0.8311 francs, while the euro inched up to US$1.0973 from its recent low of US$1.0881.
The dollar held steady on the yen at 159.14, with the risk of intervention keeping 160.00 resistance intact.
In commodity markets, oil prices held firm after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked ​Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, raising concerns about unexpected Middle East supply disruptions.
Brent futures rose 0.2% to US$94.81 a barrel, while US crude futures added 0.6% to US$84.24 a barrel.
Non-interest-bearing gold eased 0.4% to US$3,566 an ounce, having fallen almost 8% so far this month.
b6b915ba7959994d: WASHINGTON: A US judge on Wednesday barred the Federal Communications Commission from revoking Walt Disney's licenses for its eight company-owned ABC TV stations, in a dramatic blow to President Donald Trump's efforts to rein in American media companies.

"This is not a close case," US District judge Loren Alikhan wrote. ABC has a "weighty interest in 'vindicating their right to be free of retaliation for (their) protected speech,'" the judge wrote in a case that was a key test of the free-speech rights of media outlets.
The judge said the FCC appears to be carrying out a retaliatory campaign driven by Trump.
FCC chair Brendan Carr, who was tapped to lead the agency in January 2025, "has taken President Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders," the judge added.

Trump ‌has repeatedly urged broadcasters to drop comedy or news programs that he dislikes or which have been critical of him or his administration. He has also pressed the FCC on a number of occasions to revoke ABC's licenses.
Carr, the White House, Disney and ABC did not immediately respond to requests for comment late on Wednesday.

Disney and ABC sued the FCC in August to block an unprecedented early ​review of licenses for eight ABC stations, arguing that the Trump administration was trying to punish the network over its broadcast content.

Carr ordered the reviews in April, even though the ‌stations' license renewals ⁠were not scheduled to be considered before October 2028. The FCC had not ordered an early review in more than 50 years before April.
The reviews were ordered in April, a day after Trump urged ABC to ​fire late-night host Jimmy ⁠Kimmel.

Broadcast stations need FCC licenses to use public airwaves. While license revocations are extremely rare, critics say the threat of losing a license can pressure broadcasters and raise concerns about government interference in editorial and programming decisions. Networks have broad free-speech protections over programming choices.

Trump has waged an aggressive series of attacks on the news media and the latest move follows a two-year-long battle between Trump ​and Disney. In July, Trump again called for ABC stations to lose their licenses because the network refused to air a ⁠prime-time speech on elections.

The FCC is also investigating ABC daytime talk show "The View," which discusses US politics, after saying it may be subject to federal rules requiring broadcasters to provide equal-time opportunities to political candidates.
Disney ​noted earlier that as a result, the program did not invite any political candidates to appear ahead of the November midterm elections, citing the FCC's "pressure campaign."

Trump has also been more broadly criticized by free-speech advocates for attempting to target critics, deport foreign student protesters and freeze federal funds for educational institutions. His efforts have faced legal challenges and some judicial setbacks.
4d013e54f72cc2b8: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Pilots and flight crew will be subject to random drug testing under a Cabinet-approved security overhaul aimed at preventing a recurrence of large-scale drug trafficking through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has said.

In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, Saifuddin said the Cabinet had on August 19 approved a joint proposal by the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry to strengthen security controls and screening at KLIA and other international entry points following several security incidents.

“The government, through the Home Ministry and the Transport Ministry, consistently accords the highest priority to security controls at all national entry points, particularly at Kuala Lumpur International Airport,” he said.
“The action plan comprises 17 substantive recommendations formulated around three key security pillars, namely aviation security, national and border security, and physical security and protection.”
The plan will be implemented in three phases spanning more than two years.
Saifuddin said the first phase, covering a period of up to six months, would focus on “addressing gaps in security controls by making optimal use of existing statutory powers, personnel and assets”.

The measures include “tightening e-Vetting procedures for security passes, enforcing random drug testing of pilots and flight crew, periodic rotation of personnel working in restricted zones and increasing the visible presence of police personnel”.
Other proposed measures include the redeployment of narcotics detection dogs and the integration of traveller intelligence through the National Immigration Command Centre (NICC).
Saifuddin said the second phase, covering six to 24 months, would focus on “developing new capabilities and procuring strategic high-technology assets”.

These include high-powered baggage scanners, body scanners and closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems equipped with artificial intelligence (AI) analytics, as well as strengthening police canine units and enhancing specialised workforce training.
Under the third phase, spanning more than 24 months, Saifuddin said the government was committed to “comprehensively modernising and transforming the national security system”.
This would involve replacing baggage and body scanners with new-generation AI-powered equipment at all national entry points and modifying terminal and cargo infrastructure according to risk levels.

The long-term measures would also include “reinforcing the NICC as a national intelligence centre and expanding uniform and integrated security control standards across all air, land and sea entry points nationwide”, he said.

Saifuddin was responding to Bersatu’s Ketereh MP Datuk Khlir Mohd Nor, who had asked what proactive measures the ministry was taking to prevent a recurrence of large-scale drug trafficking through KLIA.
The reply did not specify whether random drug testing of pilots and flight crew had already begun.
733e596913d81a66: TOKYO: Bank of Japan (BOJ) board member Naoki Tamura said on Thursday the central bank must respond swiftly to signs of an inflation overshoot, including by accelerating the pace of interest rate hikes.
"Given that financial conditions remain accommodative, I believe the BOJ needs to bring its policy rate to a level deemed neutral to the economy soon," Tamura said in a speech.

Tamura said rising raw material costs, including higher crude oil prices due to the Middle East conflict, had led to a sharp rise in wholesale inflation, with price pressures spreading to a wide range of consumer goods.

"Recent price developments suggest further upside risks to inflation," due to uncertainty over developments in the Middle East and the yen's movements, as well as still-robust demand for AI-related goods, Tamura said.
The need for further rate hikes is heightened by the fact that Japan's inflation expectations are less firmly anchored than those of other economies, he said.

Financial conditions also remain accommodative, with surveys suggesting that the BOJ's past rate hikes and potential future increases were unlikely to inflict significant damage on corporate activity, he said.

"Within a few months of each rate hike, the BOJ can make a reasonable assessment of financial conditions based on information obtained from interviews with firms and the results of various surveys," Tamura said.

"Given that underlying CPI inflation in Japan is less firmly anchored at the BOJ's two per cent target, I believe the BOJ must respond swiftly to signs of an upward deviation in prices, including by accelerating the pace of policy interest rate hikes," he said.
36bbe12a259b6d1c: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Police investigating a controversial letter sent by Malaysia’s former intelligence chief to the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) seeking support for Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s administration ahead of the 2018 general election found no evidence of government authorisation, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has said.

In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, Saifuddin said the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) had decided against taking further action over the letter sent by the former director-general of the Malaysian External Intelligence Organisation (MEIO) on November 25 last year.
The decision came nearly two years after police submitted their investigation papers to the AGC.
“A full investigation was conducted and no instructions or authorisation from government authorities were found in this matter,” he said.
Saifuddin said police had investigated the matter under Section 8(1) of the Official Secrets Act 1972, Section 203A of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
The completed investigation papers were referred to the AGC on December 18, 2023, for scrutiny and further instructions.
“After examining the findings of the investigation submitted, the Attorney General’s Chambers on November 25, 2025, decided that no further action would be taken on this investigation,” he said.

Saifuddin was responding to Labis Member of Parliament Pang Hok Liong (PH-DAP), who had asked whether police had established if the letter was sent with the permission or at the direction of any government authority, and what the outcome of the investigation was.

The letter was signed by then MEIO director-general Datuk Hasanah Abdul Hamid and addressed to Gina Haspel of the CIA on May 4, 2018. It became public in July that year. Hasanah died in May 2023 at the age of 66.
The written reply did not elaborate on the grounds for the AGC’s decision not to pursue the case.
1971fed7ee244905: WASHINGTON, Nov 26 — US GDP growth in the third quarter was revised strongly upwards on Wednesday, with the Commerce Department citing strong investment and consumer spending, as the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge hit a three-year high in October.

US GDP growth in the third quarter this year was estimated at 4.3 per cent at an annualized rate, the department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) said, a rise of 0.9 percentage points from the previous estimate and much higher than market expectations.

“Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports,” the BEA said in a statement.

The US economy has shown resilient growth in recent months despite facing significant headwinds, including from President Donald Trump’s chaotic tariff policies and his war on Iran, which has driven up energy prices.

Also on Wednesday, the US Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge came in at a three-year high in October, according to BEA data, with a rise in energy prices accompanied by an increase in nondurable goods inflation.
The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index rose by 3.8 per cent year-on-year in October, the data showed, matching a three-year high set in May.
The US Federal Reserve has a long-term two-percent target for PCE inflation, one that it has missed for almost six years.
In September, the Fed raised interest rates for the first time in three years in order to combat the persistent price increases, which have battered US households and businesses.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held rates steady at its last meeting in October, but with inflation continuing to run hot, it is likely to raise rates at its next confab in December.
The years of above-target inflation since the pandemic have hit US households hard, with current price levels more than 30 per cent higher than in 2020, as per the official Consumer Price Index.
Affordability was a key issue in this month’s midterm elections, which saw Trump’s Republican Party swept out of power in both houses of Congress by their rival Democrats.
The price increases have been driven by Trump’s tariffs, energy price increases due to the war on Iran and a massive investment boom in AI technology driving up demand for some goods.
Trump has defended his economic performance by pointing to data like GDP growth, which has been robust despite the headwinds, mainly on the back of the AI boom.
Economists warn that while consumer spending has remained strong, despite the high prices, there is a growing divide between lower- and higher-income households in the United States.
Beige Book’

The Fed’s latest “Beige Book,” released Wednesday, said US consumers grappling with high consumer prices have been “increasingly selective” in discretionary purchases. Auto sales weakened in a move the report attributed to higher energy prices, while lofty lending rates were a drag on the housing market.
On the positive side, the report said employment levels “rose slightly,” with contacts in several sectors citing “steady or rising labour demand.”
Of the 12 districts across the country, eight reported “slight to moderate” growth while four reported no change, the Fed report said.
Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, said the fresh inflation data pointed to a likely rate hike in December, and possibly another a month later.
“America’s inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock,” she said. “The Federal Reserve has to act in December and likely January.”
She pointed out that while consumer spending did increase in absolute terms in October, it was flat once adjusted for inflation.

Ryan Sweet, chief global economist at Oxford Economics, said the strong GDP data would give Fed policymakers room to breathe when it comes to further rate hikes, which tend to cool economic activity as they tackle inflation.
“The tightening in financial market conditions, if sustained, will not have a noticeable impact on growth until the second half of next year,” he said. — AFP
2252989ed561584c: JOHOR BARU: The High Court has acquitted and discharged two men charged with trafficking more than 2kg of methamphetamine four years ago.

Judicial Commissioner Avinder Singh Gill Ranjit Singh ruled that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against D. Thanasilan, 38, and I. Yuvaraj, 26, at the close of its case. Both men were therefore not required to enter their defence.
In his grounds of judgment, Avinder said the prosecution had failed to prove custody and control, knowledge, possession and trafficking of the drugs, as well as common intention between the accused.

He also cited material inconsistencies in the testimony of a prosecution witness who was part of the raiding team, the failure to produce relevant exhibits and the vehicle, the inability to rule out third-party access, and gaps in the chain of evidence.
"The court rejected the witness's explanation that discrepancies in the alleged transfer of the drugs were merely mistakes, as they went to the heart of the prosecution's case.
"During cross-examination, the witness admitted that he did not see which accused opened the Proton Waja, who carried the bag containing the drugs or who placed it inside the car.

"The court also noted conflicting evidence over whether the second accused, Yuvaraj, had transferred a red plastic bag into the Proton Waja. The key to the car, allegedly seized from Thanasilan's shorts, was also not produced in court.
"No fingerprint or DNA evidence linked either accused to the Proton Waja or the drug exhibits," he said.
According to the charge, the two men were jointly accused of trafficking 2,145.68g of methamphetamine in front of a workshop in Jalan Bunga Tanjung, Kulai, at 8.40pm on June 8, 2022.
They were charged under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Umar Faiz Abdul Kohar called six witnesses during the trial.
Thanasilan was represented by Mohd Daud Ismail, while Yuvaraj was represented by K.L. Chee & Co.

116f62c4c6f3d46d: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The government will study whether to set up a fund to share the economic gains from artificial intelligence (AI) with Malaysians, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said last night.

Anwar said he had asked the Communications and Digital ministries to study the options, including a proposal by US Senator Bernie Sanders for legislation to establish an AI fund that would pay dividends to Americans.
“I agree in principle. We can start engaging now, even before legislation is in place. For example, when we set a minimum wage, multinational companies have to comply too.

“At first, they objected, saying they came to Malaysia because wages were low. That may have been true 30 years ago. They now have to accept that living standards have risen,” he said on RTM’s Dialog Negara programme on TV1 last night.
The programme was also simulcast on Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
Anwar said Malaysia imposed firm conditions on foreign AI investors, including requirements to provide water supply infrastructure and train Malaysians in advanced AI skills.
The Prime Minister cited what he described as a US$15 billion investment by Google.

He said the conditions included spending RM600 million on water supply infrastructure in Negeri Sembilan and providing advanced AI training for 1,000 young Malaysians, with Universiti Malaya as an example of a potential training partner.
“If the conditions are too onerous, investors may stay away. We should make clear that we welcome investment while taking firm steps to keep inequality from widening,” he said.
Anwar said governments had a role in ensuring the benefits of growth were more widely shared across the economy.
The spread of AI made that more urgent because it could deepen inequality, he said.

On the impact of AI on jobs, Anwar said rapid technological change and unexpected shocks could bring challenges, including financial pressures. He said people could anticipate those problems and devise solutions.
He said government departments and the private sector should receive support to create new jobs as technology evolves.

The Dialog Negara panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.

Also on the panel were PlusVibes Group founder and chief executive Dr Madiha Fuad, Farm Fresh Berhad group chief operating officer Azmi Zainal, independent preacher Izzhar Nazri, Architects of Diversity (AOD) Malaysia founder Jason Wee, and Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Student Representative Council president Mohamad Adib Hazim Mohamad Razali. — Bernama
fdf84b4e282dc60b: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — From traditional Japanese mochi desserts such as dango and warabi mochi to more recent Korean-style trends like the deeply caramelised butter tteok, we have developed a lively love affair with these chewy treats made from glutinous rice flour.

The latest viral hit, the mochi crêpe, is heavily driven by its ASMR-ready design: Imagine snapping the thin, crisp chocolate shell of a rectangular patty to reveal layers of chewy rice mochi, cream and crunchy nuts.
It’s that stark textural contrast of this Korean-style delight that tempts foodies, the shattering of the outer chocolate shell followed by the gooey stretch of the mochi within.
Then there is the unexpected but undeniable delectable juxtaposition of rich cream and some crackly element.

In the case of the Kunafa Mochi Crêpe by TBX (The Baking Xperiment), that crackly element comes in the form of the now omnipresent kunafa — fine, hairly-like strands of toasted kataifi or shredded phyllo dough.

You know this ingredient from the popular Dubai chocolate trend, of course; the filling has incredible longevity, being used in everything from the original Middle Eastern dessert to chewy Dubai cookies.
Those looking for an assortment of flavours to try can check out the trinity of mochi crêpes by home-based baker Ten.Half10.5: strawberry, pistachio and chocolate are available.

This distinction happens to be the main variable, as far as I can tell: beyond nutty inclusions like pistachio and hazelnut or fruity compotes, other flavours for the fillings range from vividly green matcha to espresso-based ganache.

The mochi core and the thin chocolate shell appear to be constants; though the latter could be livened up by substituting white chocolate or dark chocolate. Perhaps a light dusting of organic cacao powder or matcha over the chocolate shell to finish.
As this trend continues to take off in Malaysia, expect to see more local flavours and twists to the original recipe. Kaya and salted butter, perhaps? Or Musang King durian?
(I, for one, hope to see Cake Jalan Tiung come out with a pandan and gula Melaka mochi crêpe, a nod to their signature Pandan & Gula Melaka Croissant.)

For something more sophisticated, Cake Tella’s mochi crêpe pairs dark chocolate cream and hazelnuts. This comes in a set of two: one version is infused with Jameson Whisky; the other is alcohol-free and has hazelnut feuilletine.

Whichever style strikes your fancy, don’t forget to savour the sudden shattering of the chocolate shell and the slow, supple stretch of the mochi. Or, to borrow from a famous cereal slogan: “Snap, Crackle... Pull Apart!”
For more food fables and café chronicles, visit Life for Beginners.

6221ae85a806081e: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described corruption in the country as a systemic issue that requires the sustained commitment and firm resolve of all parties to eradicate it, including by fostering an awareness of integrity among the younger generation.
He noted that the fight against corruption is no easy task, given that the practice has become deeply entrenched within the system.
Therefore, he said the government must continue to take decisive action, without allowing the pursuit of popularity to be a primary consideration.

“Corruption in this country has become systemic. That is what I inherited. We have to stand firm and keep going, whether it’s popular or not. Popularity is secondary,” he said on RTM’s Dialog Negara programme on TV1 last night, which was also simulcast on RTMKlik, Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.

Anwar said fighting corruption had proved harder than expected, making it all the more important to instil a sense of integrity from an early age, as young people could drive change and help secure Malaysia’s future.
He said he had reached out to young people through various programmes, including meetings at higher education institutions, to encourage them to make integrity a guiding principle.
“We want them to hold on to their ideals. They are our hope. If we can convince Gen Z and Gen Y of the importance of integrity, our future will be more secure. That is my hope,” he said.

Asked about allegations that influential people linked to corruption received preferential treatment, Anwar said the rule of law must be upheld, and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) must be free to investigate without interference from interested parties.
He cited the case of his former senior political secretary, Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, who was charged in a corruption case. Anwar said he had stayed out of the investigation.

“When someone close to me is being investigated, of course I ask what it’s about. He told me, and I said I wouldn’t interfere. He was then charged. Has anything like that happened before? No. My Cabinet colleagues know I won’t defend anyone involved in corruption,” he said.
Looking ahead to 2027, Anwar said he hoped all Malaysians would carry out their responsibilities with integrity so that the country’s development continued to be guided by that principle.
He said students, families and the wider community all had a part in building the country, alongside leaders and civil servants.

“Our problems are about principles and conduct. We shouldn’t hate one another or see these problems through the lens of race. We have to put things right together and build on our strengths. As I’ve said, we have tremendous potential to raise Malaysia’s standing,” he said.

The Dialog Negara panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.

The panel also included PlusVibes Group founder and chief executive Dr Madiha Fuad, Farm Fresh Berhad group chief operating officer Azmi Zainal, independent preacher Izzhar Nazri, Architects of Diversity (AOD) Malaysia founder Jason Wee, and Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Student Representative Council president Mohamad Adib Hazim Mohamad Razali. — Bernama
dba7e63676e0042b: KUALA LUMPUR: Road tax rates for electric vehicles (EVs) are, on average, 85 per cent lower than those for internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles under the new rates that took effect on Jan 1.
In a written parliamentary reply, the Transport Ministry said the lower rates were aimed at encouraging consumers to switch to zero-emission vehicles.
It said 174,686 EVs were registered as of August, including 130,229 passenger cars, accounting for 74.6 per cent of total registrations.
The ministry said road tax rates for private vehicles were based on their powertrain systems — engine capacity for ICE vehicles and motor power for EVs.
"For private ICE vehicles, road tax is calculated based on engine capacity in cubic centimetres (cc).
"For EVs, motor power in watts determines the road tax rate, which increases with higher motor output," it said.

The ministry was responding to Mohd Azizi Abu Naim (Independent-Gua Musang), who asked whether the government would consider restructuring EV road tax rates based on vehicle segment, prestige and performance, in addition to motor power in kilowatts (kW).
The ministry said higher electric motor power generally corresponded with higher vehicle prices and larger, heavier vehicles.
As such, motor power remained the basis for EV road tax rates, with the existing structure established following a comprehensive study.
1118a2186df48e91: LISBON, Nov 26 — New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino insisted his team would find a way to win games after a tricky start to life at the helm of the Red Devils.
United were held to a chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, after a 4-0 thrashing by rivals Liverpool in his first match on Sunday.
Man United, 19th in the Premier League, were upset with several refereeing decisions across both matches, but Pochettino said his team had to take responsibility for their situation.
“I’m happy to be here,” said Pochettino, when asked about the various decisions that had gone against his team in his first week in charge.
“We are here to take responsibility... we are going for sure to improve and to put that team in the place that, because of their history, we deserve to be.

“Nothing is easy but we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and most importantly the players and the power and the energy from our fans that is massive and I think united, all together, I think we will find a way to perform and win games.”

United had two goals controversially ruled out against Sporting, but might have won the game were it not for a mistake from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. The Belgian dropped the ball for Colombian striker Luis Suarez to score his second goal of the night, cancelling out Bruno Fernandes’s double against his old side.
Lammens also saved a Suarez penalty and then gave away a second penalty, this time scored by the striker.
“This type of thing happens, that is football,” said Pochettino. “Football is about making mistakes – I’m going to support always my player if something happens.”
The Argentine said Man United’s defenders might have done better to help protect Lammens before he spilled the ball.
“When you are a ‘keeper, it’s not easy, that ball. And always you need help from your teammates,” added Pochettino.
“But of course, we need to accept, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve in all the small details that for sure we will improve.” — AFP
d117e54039f2fe72: KOTA KINABALU: Lapan daerah di Pantai Timur Sabah terputus bekalan elektrik pagi ini, menurut notis pemakluman Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd.
Notis pemakluman rasmi syarikat itu memberitahu daerah terlibat adalah Tawau, Sandakan, Semporna, Lahad Datu, Kunak, Beluran, Telupid, dan Kinabatangan.
“Pihak Sabah Electricity sedang mengenal pasti punca gangguan dan seterusnya melaksanakan pemulihan secara berperingkat.
“Sabah Electricity amat menghargai kesabaran anda dan segala kesulitan amat dikesali, terima kasih,” katanya.
Punca kejadian masih disiasat, bagaimanapun ia dipercayai berpunca daripada sebuah menara penghantaran bekalan elektrik tumbang di daerah Ranau.

Sementara itu di media sosial, tular video kejadian berdurasi 1 minit 51 saat menunjukkan kabel penghantaran elektrik merentas jalan di daerah Ranau akibat menara penghantaran terletak berhampiran tumbang.

“Bilik gerakan telah diaktifkan dan pasukan teknikal sedang melaksanakan usaha pemulihan bekalan elektrik terutama di Sandakan, Tawau dan Lahad Datu secara berperingkat,” katanya.
Menurutnya punca sebenar kejadian sedang dikenal pasti.
684facb2f6bc9626: SEOUL: South Korea's central bank raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 3.25 per cent on Thursday, resuming its tightening cycle after an October pause as an AI-fuelled export boom keeps growth brisk and inflation above target.
The seven-member monetary policy board voted to raise the seven-day repurchase rate to its highest since November 2024, a decision forecast by 32 of 34 analysts surveyed by Reuters.
Governor Shin Hyun Song will hold a news conference at 0210 GMT.
d8fbda58d439ab98: KOTA KINABALU: Tourism-related industries provided employment to 415,100 people in Sabah last year, an increase of 7.1 per cent from 387,600 in the previous year.
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said nearly one in four employed people in the state worked in tourism-related industries.
"Nearly one in every four employed people in Sabah is involved in tourism-related industries.
"This clearly shows that tourism is not merely an industry, but also a source of economic activity and livelihood for hundreds of thousands of people in Sabah.

"These figures give the state government and industry players confidence to continue strengthening investment, developing tourism products and encouraging greater participation by local communities," he said in a statement.

He said the publication of the Sabah Regional Tourism Satellite Account 2025 was an initiative by his ministry, in collaboration with the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), to provide more comprehensive and authoritative data on the state's tourism sector.
The data showed that Sabah's tourism industry generated RM14.4 billion in value added in 2025, recording growth of 5.6 per cent.
The sector contributed 12.3 per cent to the state's economy, up from 11.9 per cent in the previous year.
Domestic tourism consumption also increased by 14.2 per cent to RM13.4 billion, compared with RM11.7 billion in 2024.
Inbound tourism expenditure rose by 20.8 per cent to RM7.5 billion, while domestic tourism expenditure grew by 6.8 per cent to RM5.9 billion.

Jafry said the publication was an important step towards strengthening data-driven planning and policymaking, while enabling the ministry to measure more accurately the tourism industry's contribution to the state's economy and people's livelihoods.
a7450767ebd42d0f: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Three districts on Sabah’s east coast — Sandakan, Tawau and Lahad Datu — were hit by power outages early this morning following an incident involving the electricity transmission system.
Sabah Electricity said in a statement that the disruption occurred at 6.04am, with efforts underway to restore supply in stages.
An operations centre was being activated to coordinate restoration work across the three districts.
The utility provider acknowledged the impact of the disruption on daily life, business operations and community activities, and apologised to affected consumers.
“Our priority now is to restore electricity supply as quickly as possible without compromising the safety and stability of the system,” Sabah Electricity said.
The cause of the incident remains under investigation, with updates on restoration efforts to be issued through the company’s official channels.
Sabah Electricity did not disclose how many consumers were affected or give an estimated timeline for full restoration.
d5bdc4a7048f10d5: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 850 people were detained and 620 prosecutions were recorded under Section 55E of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for allowing undocumented migrants to enter or remain on premises between 2025 and Sept 17 this year.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Immigration Department records showed 691 complaints involving residential homes were received last year.
Enforcement operations during the period led to the arrest of 8,453 undocumented migrants.
"During the same period, 96 people were arrested under Section 55E, while 391 prosecutions were recorded," he said in a written parliamentary reply published on the Parliament website.
From Jan 1 to Sept 17 this year, the department received 109 complaints involving residential premises and detained 6,581 undocumented migrants during enforcement operations.
Saifuddin said 131 people were arrested under Section 55E during the period, with 229 prosecutions recorded.

He was responding to Dr Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas), who asked for a breakdown of complaints, prosecutions and action against homeowners or tenants renting premises to Rohingya and other undocumented migrants.
Section 55E prohibits anyone with an interest in, or management or control of, premises from allowing undocumented migrants to enter or remain there.
Upon conviction, offenders face a fine of RM5,000 to RM30,000, imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both, for each undocumented migrant found on the premises.
For a second or subsequent conviction, the penalty increases to a fine of RM10,000 to RM60,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both, for each migrant.
Saifuddin said the government viewed seriously any act of allowing undocumented migrants to enter or remain on premises, including rented homes.

He said the department would continue to step up intelligence gathering, inspections and targeted operations, and take stern action against those found allowing undocumented migrants to stay on properties under their management or control.
e692aaf3eb11b641: PETALING JAYA: To some, the title "Sasterawan Negara" would be a crowning achievement. To A Samad Said, it was not something worth holding on to at all costs - particularly when others called for it to be revoked.

“Soal tarik balik anugerah Sasterawan Negara itu sangat bapak alu-alukan. Teruskanlah (I wholeheartedly welcome the matter of revoking the National Laureate award. Go right ahead)," he reportedly said.
Better known as Pak Samad, the celebrated novelist, poet and journalist passed away on Nov 24 at age 91, leaving behind a literary legacy that spanned more than seven decades.

While his name will forever be associated with some of the most influential works in modern Malay literature, his life was also defined by a willingness to speak up for causes he believed in, even when doing so invited criticism and controversy.

Awarded the Sasterawan Negara title in 1985, Samad was the fourth recipient of Malaysia’s highest literary honour, which recognises writers who have made outstanding and lasting contributions to Malay-language literature.
He stood out for his versatility, earning acclaim across literary forms, from novels and poetry to plays, short stories and essays.

For Samad, however, such recognition was never more important than the principles for which he stood. This became particularly apparent in 2009, when he joined the movement opposing the policy of teaching and learning science and mathematics in English (PPSMI).
At a press conference at the Kelantan menteri besar’s official residence in February that year, he said he was prepared to relinquish his National Laureate title.
"I am willing to have the title taken away if it means my mother tongue is preserved. There is no point in holding on to the title because it is not a permanent possession.
“I am a ‘People’s Laureate’ who will continue to fight for the future generations of the Malay community,” he said.
His resolve was put to the test again in 2013, following his involvement in the controversial display of the Sang Saka Malaya flag during a Merdeka Eve gathering.
He faced calls from prominent figures for his literary title to be revoked and was subsequently detained and questioned by police under the Sedition Act. But Samad remained unfazed.
Speaking to Astro Awani on Sept 5, 2013, he said: “The title of National Laureate is only for this world and cannot be taken to the afterlife.”
Even in his later years, Samad remained actively involved in national issues, becoming a prominent figure in the Bersih electoral reform movement.

Recognisable by his long white beard, flowing hair and woven songkok, he joined peaceful rallies, championed democratic reform, and used poetry to give voice to concerns over social justice and the country’s future.
Among his protest poems were “Unggun Bersih”, “Janji Demokrasi” and “Di Atas Padang Sejarah”.

Through his extensive body of work, Samad explored the human condition, reaching generations of Malaysians, including students who encountered his works through school reading lists. Several of his works have been translated into other languages, bringing Malaysian literature to readers beyond the country’s borders.
Ultimately, A Samad Said may have been honoured for his words, but he will also be remembered for having the courage to stand behind them.
6ae2ef9ab6c789eb: PETALING JAYA: Nazri Aziz is prepared to take on Wawasan's Padang Rengas MP Azahari Hasan as the Umno man seeks to regain the parliamentary seat he once held for six terms in the next general election (GE16).

Nazri said Wawasan cannot use the incumbency rule as its basis to contest the seat under the Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional alliance, because Azahari won the seat in the 2022 general election while in Bersatu.
"The incumbency principle in seat negotiations refers to the party, not the individual. When we negotiate the distribution of seats, we look at the party that won the seat in the last election.
"At Padang Rengas, the party that won the seat in GE15 was Bersatu, not Wawasan," he said in an interview with FMT.
The former Umno Supreme Council member said Wawasan, therefore, could not claim Padang Rengas as its seat to contest in GE16 simply because Azahari had joined the party.
He said Padang Rengas had been Umno's traditional seat since it was created in 1974.
PAS did not contest the seat in 2022 when BN came in second to PN.
"So, if we cooperate with PAS in GE16, BN should be the one contesting Padang Rengas," he said, expressing confidence that an understanding could be reached between Umno and PAS.
"If Azahari wants to contest, that's his right. If he wants to contest on a Wawasan ticket, by all means, go ahead. I have no problem contesting against him.
"But he should not assume that just because Wawasan is now in PN, the Padang Rengas seat is automatically theirs," he said.
Earlier this month, Azahari maintained that he would not make way for BN in Padang Rengas, after Nazri voiced his intention to make his electoral return.
However, Azahari, who joined Wawasan after being sacked by Bersatu in February, did not dismiss the possibility of a seat exchange between BN and PN.
In GE15, Azahari won the seat with a 3,046-vote majority, defeating his closest contender, BN candidate Arrif Majid.
Nazri had decided not to contest the election that year after six terms as Padang Rengas MP. At the time, he said he would be retiring from politics.
76bd705ae93118e2: PETALING JAYA: Nazri Aziz menolak alasan Wawasan mahu mempertahankan Padang Rengas berdasarkan prinsip penyandang, sambil menegaskan kerusi itu dimenangi Bersatu pada PRU15, bukannya parti berkenaan.

Bekas ahli Majlis Kerja Tertinggi (MKT) Umno berkata, prinsip penyandang dalam rundingan pembahagian kerusi sepatutnya merujuk kepada parti yang memenangi pilihan raya terdahulu, bukan individu yang kemudian bertukar parti.
“Penyandang itu merujuk kepada parti, bukannya individu. Apabila kita berunding mengenai pembahagian kerusi, kita melihat parti memenangi kerusi berkenaan pada pilihan raya sebelumnya.
“Di Padang Rengas, parti yang menang pada PRU15 ialah Bersatu, bukannya Wawasan,” katanya dalam temu bual FMT.
Bekas Ahli Parlimen Padang Rengas menekankan, Wawasan tidak boleh menganggap kerusi berkenaan sebagai haknya semata-mata kerana penyandang, Azahari Hasan, kini menyertai parti komponen PN itu.
Menurutnya, kerusi Padang Rengas diwujudkan pada 1974 merupakan kerusi tradisi Barisan Nasional (BN) sebelum dimenangi calon Bersatu atas tiket PN pada PRU15.

Beliau berkata, PAS tidak bertanding di kawasan berkenaan pada pilihan raya lalu manakala BN menduduki tempat kedua, justeru Umno wajar diberi keutamaan jika kerjasama pilihan raya dengan PAS diteruskan pada PRU16.
“Jadi, kalau kita bekerjasama dengan PAS pada PRU16, sudah tentulah BN yang patut bertanding di Padang Rengas,” katanya.

Pada 13 Nov lalu, Azahari bertegas tidak akan menyerahkan Padang Rengas kepada BN dan mahu mempertahankannya atas tiket PN pada PRU16 berdasarkan prinsip penyandang, mengulas hasrat Nazri kembali ke kerusi itu.

Azahari yang menyertai Wawasan selepas dipecat Bersatu pada Februari lalu berkata, keputusan akhir mengenai pembahagian kerusi perlu diserahkan kepada pucuk pimpinan gabungan, selain tidak menolak kemungkinan pertukaran kerusi menerusi rundingan.
Pada PRU15, Azahari menewaskan calon BN Arrif Majid dengan majoriti 3,046 undi.
Pertikaian itu turut mencetuskan persoalan mengenai rundingan kerusi BN-PN pada PRU16, susulan kerjasama kedua-dua gabungan dalam PRN Negeri Sembilan dan Melaka.

Nazri yang mahu kembali bertanding di Padang Rengas atas tiket BN berkata, beliau mempunyai ramai kenalan dalam PAS dan yakin persefahaman mengenai kerusi berkenaan dapat dicapai jika kedua-dua parti bekerjasama.
“Kalau Azahari mahu bertanding, bertandinglah. Itu hak dia. Kalau mahu bertanding atas tiket Wawasan, silakan. Saya tidak ada masalah untuk berlawan dengannya.
“Tetapi janganlah beliau beranggapan kerana Wawasan sekarang berada dalam PN, kerusi Padang Rengas secara automatik menjadi hak mereka,” katanya.
776879bce5ed55f3: SINGAPORE, Nov 26 — Civil servants in Singapore will receive a 1.55-month year-end bonus, marking the public sector’s largest year-end payout in two decades, alongside targeted cash top-ups of up to S$600 (RM1,914) for junior-grade officers, the Public Service Division (PSD) announced on Wednesday.

Coupled with the 0.45-month payout disbursed in July, the announcement lifts the total Annual Variable Component (AVC) for 2026 to exactly two months. All public officers will concurrently receive the standard one-month non-pensionable annual allowance, commonly referred to as the 13th-month bonus, payable in December, according to CNA.

The bumper payout reflects Singapore’s upgraded 2026 gross domestic product growth forecast of around 6 per cent, as well as National Wages Council guidelines urging employers to reward staff amid better-than-expected economic performance.

State economists attributed the buoyant expansion to robust third-quarter trade alongside “expectations that the global boom in AI-related investment would continue for the rest of the year, thus benefiting sectors like manufacturing and wholesale trade in Singapore”.

To cushion lower-to-middle income civil servants against stubborn cost-of-living pressures, the government introduced tiered lump-sum subsidies. Public officers in grades equivalent to MX13(I) and MX14 will receive an additional one-off payment of S$300, while those in grades MX15 and MX16, along with personnel under the Operations Support Scheme, will receive a higher disbursement of S$600.

The compensation package was finalised following consultations with public sector unions. National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) deputy secretary-general Cham Hui Fong said the labour movement sought to “recognise fairly our civil servants’ dedication and contributions in delivering critical public services amid a rapidly evolving global environment”, noting that such “progressive and targeted support will provide greater assistance to officers who may need it more amid cost-of-living pressures”.

Highlighting the structural challenges accompanying digital disruption, Cham added: “We thank all civil servants for their professionalism and commitment in serving Singapore and Singaporeans. Even as Singapore’s economy has performed well, external uncertainties and structural shifts, particularly from AI and digitalisation, remain.
“We encourage our public officers to embrace new technologies and training so that they remain adaptable and future-ready.”

Echoing support, Amalgamated Union of Public Employees general secretary Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari described the full-year package as “a meaningful recognition of the hard work, dedication and contributions of our civil servants throughout the year”, stressing that the supplementary payments reaffirm the state’s commitment to uplifting lower-grade frontline staff.
0f4b8b80ed036321: KOTA KINABALU: Eight districts on the east coast of Sabah are experiencing a power outage this morning, according to Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd.
In a notice on its official Facebook page, Sabah Electricity said the affected districts are Tawau, Sandakan, Semporna, Lahad Datu, Kunak, Beluran, Telupid and Kinabatangan.
"Sabah Electricity is identifying the cause of the disruption and working on a phased restoration of power.
"Sabah Electricity greatly appreciates your patience and regrets any inconvenience caused," it said.
While the cause of the incident is still under investigation, it is believed to have stemmed from the collapse of an electricity transmission tower in the Ranau district.
4abb64999e075459: KUALA LUMPUR: Four paintings linked to the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) scandal are expected to go on public display at the National Art Gallery as early as the end of this year, nearly a year after their return to Malaysia.
The exhibition, organised by the National Art Gallery, will allow the public to view works by some of the world's most renowned artists, including Pablo Picasso.
It is understood that preparations are underway, including efforts to verify the paintings' authenticity and ownership status.
The exhibition is expected to be a major cultural event, showcasing the works' artistic and historical significance while documenting their links to one of Malaysia's biggest financial scandals.

The four paintings recovered by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) are Joan Miró's Composition (1953), Maurice Utrillo's Maison de rendez-vous, rue Saint-Rustique, Montmartre (1934), Balthus's Étude pour femme couchée (1948) and Pablo Picasso's L'Ecuyère et les clowns (1961).
In a response to Berita Harian, the National Art Gallery confirmed that discussions and preparations were underway, although no exhibition date had been finalised.
It said it was working with several agencies, including the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry, Finance Ministry and MACC, to organise the exhibition.
"The latest meeting involving both ministries, MACC, the National Financial Crime Prevention Centre (NFCC) and the National Visual Arts Development Board (LPSVN) was held on Oct 21.
"The meeting discussed the ownership status of the 1MDB-linked artworks and outlined further plans," it said.
The gallery said the main challenge was establishing ownership of the paintings, which had been discussed at the meeting.
"Key processes that must first be completed include verifying the authenticity of the works and determining their actual ownership before conservation experts can conduct further inspections.
"This is important to ensure each painting is examined and handled in accordance with established art preservation procedures and standards," it said.
The gallery added that the market value of all four paintings had been assessed by international auction houses Christie's and Sotheby's in the United States.
It was also conducting its own valuation as part of the documentation process.
In April, it was reported that the four high-value paintings had been brought back to Malaysia and placed under secure custody at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya.

The paintings were among assets recovered through the government's efforts to reclaim funds and property linked to the 1MDB scandal, involving cooperation between local enforcement agencies and international partners.
The MACC had said their return reflected Malaysia's continued efforts to recover misappropriated assets and strengthen its position in international asset recovery practices.
Meanwhile, efforts are underway to bring back another seven artworks linked to 1MDB that are being held by Christie's in the United States.

In was reported in December last year that 12 valuable paintings and masterpieces by renowned artists, worth about US$30 million (RM140 million), would be displayed at the National Art Gallery once they arrived in Malaysia.
Another six paintings previously owned by 1MDB case witness Jasmine Loo remain under Christie's custody and can only be handed over through a US court order.
To date, Malaysia has recovered about RM31.2 billion in assets linked to 1MDB, representing nearly 70 per cent of the total identified assets.

5a1f64496bc9ce6d: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Three men suspected of assaulting a 62-year-old man following a road accident in Kuala Terengganu were seen smiling and laughing as they arrived at court yesterday, with one even raising a clenched fist towards a cameraman.

According to Harian Metro, the suspects, aged between 39 and 44, were brought to the Kuala Terengganu Magistrates’ Court for remand proceedings after footage of the alleged attack went viral on social media.
Their behaviour in front of the cameras drew further criticism on social media, with users questioning whether the men had any respect for their elders.

The suspects were remanded for four days to assist investigations under Section 325 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt, which carries a prison sentence of up to seven years, with offenders also liable to a fine upon conviction.
The incident occurred on Monday in Lorong Ikhwan, Jalan Pasir Panjang, when a Perodua Alza allegedly crashed into the rear of a Skoda driven by a woman.
The victim, identified as Roslan Ngah, was allegedly assaulted in the aftermath of the collision.
Footage of the alleged attack subsequently circulated widely on social media, prompting public condemnation.
e28cf856e4894c28: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the success of Farm Fresh Bhd, which received initial capital support from Khazanah Nasional Bhd, as an example to drive the development of potential companies and ensure the sustainability of the country’s food industry.

He said that the approach of supporting high-potential companies at an early stage before transitioning them into new entities once their businesses have matured and achieved success should serve as a reference point for strengthening the country’s food security.

“We are proud that Farm Fresh is not only here but also in several other countries, and we have recorded success in terms of producing food products and being able to control prices as quickly as possible and get revenue due to exports and investments abroad,” he said on Radio Televisyen Malaysia’s Dialog Negara Khas Bersama Perdana Menteri: Di Sebalik Keputusan last night.

Anwar was responding to a question from Farm Fresh group chief operating officer Azmi Zainal on how the government balances consumer protection while supporting the viability of food producers in the face of rising production costs due to global uncertainty.

At the same time, he stressed that the country’s food and agricultural industries are facing tremendous pressure due to global geopolitical uncertainties, including conflicts involving Iran, Israel and the United States, and the Russia-Ukraine war.
Shipping costs have risen by 10 times, which has increased the cost of imported inputs such as phosphates that pass through strategic routes such as the Strait of Hormuz.

“All countries in Asia and even in Europe are now facing political and social tensions due to rising prices of goods, partly due to national fiscal policies and partly due to the problem of rising imported goods,” he said.

Therefore, to balance consumer welfare and producer viability, the classic weaknesses of the agriculture, livestock and fisheries sectors need to be addressed aggressively by relevant agencies through access to early capital such as Agrobank.

Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said focus should also be given to increasing production through adequate supply of inputs including fertilisers, in addition to marketing infrastructure reforms.
The Prime Minister also stressed that the channelling of large funds must be accompanied by strict governance to combat leakage and a culture of commission.

“Governance must not be neglected, as excessive leakages of funds can lead to a situation where the problem becomes deeply systemic. When we eventually take action, the backlash is severe and the anger widespread because those involved have become accustomed to receiving commissions,” he said. — Bernama
134d98410ef7ff52: WASHINGTON: The US has approved the sale of maintenance equipment and other items to Ukraine for its fleet of F-16 fighter jets, a transaction worth US$622 million financed by European partners, the State Department announced Wednesday.
The funding comes from Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway, the state department said in a statement, underlining that "there will be no US funds associated with this transfer."

It said the package includes "Cartridge Actuated Device/Propellant Actuated Devices; lab equipment; and transportation support," which will be added to a smaller previous sale below the limit required to be reported to Congress.

"The proposed sale will improve Ukraine's capability to meet current and future threats by further equipping it to conduct self-defence and regional security missions with a more robust air defence capability," the statement said.

The Wall Street Journal reported in early October that delays in maintenance and a shortage of parts had grounded more than half of Ukraine's fleet, and all of its US-made aircraft could be affected by year-end.
Ukrainian officials denied there were any dire issues with aircraft availability but admitted that certain components for the F-16s were no longer in production and harder to source.
Kyiv pushed its Western allies for it to be given advanced fighter jets after Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022 and finally received its first batch of F-16s two years later.
df6aaa8ce16db75d: CAIRO, Nov 26 — A fire erupted in Egyptian capital Cairo on Wednesday killing at least 31 people, the health ministry said, after a fuel truck reportedly overturned on a packed highway.

AFP footage showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists sounded their horns and scrambled to get away. Surrounding buildings appeared to escape the flames.

State media reported that the fire broke out when a truck loaded with fuel overturned on Cairo’s Ring Road – a crowded highway linking different parts of the capital – and burst into flames, engulfing nearby vehicles.
The health ministry said 39 ambulances were sent to the scene and 15 people were taken to hospital with injuries, four of them in critical condition.
“The scene was terrifying,” Abdel Rahman Khalil told AFP, saying he arrived shortly after the crash and saw the overturned fuel truck engulfed in flames.
AFP images showed a grisly aftermath with cars burned out, as firefighters doused the truck’s wreckage.
Egypt’s public prosecutor said an investigation had been opened and DNA tests were being carried out to identify badly burned victims.
The health ministry said it had raised its emergency alert level and Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar had travelled to the scene and nearby hospitals.
Charred wreckage
The health minister’s spokesman told state-linked al-Qahera News that “the Ring Road has been reopened, and the remnants of the accident have been cleared.”
Footage carried by Al-Qahera News showed the charred truck’s wreckage being removed, while traffic partially resumed around it.
A spokesperson for the Egyptian Cabinet told local media that Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly had ordered an investigation into the causes of the accident.

He said the government was awaiting a full clarification before determining “future measures regarding the transport of petroleum products and ensuring safety and security during such transport operations”.
Road deaths
Egypt, with its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, has suffered several deadly fires in recent years.
Fire escapes, smoke detectors and alarms are rare and in many areas, warrens of narrow roads make it hard for fire engines to reach disaster sites.
Car crashes are also common, and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted.
Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency.
The year before, more than 5,200 road deaths were recorded across the country, according to authorities.
In August, at least 18 people, many of them teenagers, were killed in northern Egypt when two pick-up trucks carrying agricultural day-labourers crashed. — AFP
d0f112a32145143c: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The government will consider introducing stricter regulations to control the entry of cheap goods through international e-commerce platforms, especially from China, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, said the influx of foreign products affects the macro economy and directly undermines the competitiveness of local entrepreneurs.
“I agree, and I think we should introduce stricter regulations,” he said on Radio Televisyen Malaysia’s (RTM) special Di Sebalik Keputusan... Dialog Negara programme aired last night.

The prime minister responded to Chunk & Dunk’s founder, Adam Shamil, on how the government balances competition from cheap international e-commerce goods on platforms such as Pinduoduo and Temu to protect local entrepreneurs and brands.
However, Anwar said the government will not completely block or restrict these foreign platforms, but the quality and standards of the products sold must be monitored, including their halal status.

“This is why we are starting to impose some restrictions now. We will give them the opportunity to enter on the condition that local companies are involved or that they provide guarantees of quality and health. And, if it is labelled halal, it must be guaranteed as halal,” he said.

Anwar said the matter was also raised with China’s leaders during several visits to the country, and Chinese President Xi Jinping informed of China’s readiness to increase space for Malaysian export goods.
“We do not intend to restrict, but what we want is investment and trade, not an influx of cheap goods... and this is killing smaller companies.
“So, we have agreed in the Cabinet to take several steps to curb slightly, but not completely restrict, because this goes against our (trade) policy to allow increased imports,” he said.
At the same time, Anwar also reminded the people not to be mesmerised by advertisements for products whose quality has not been guaranteed.
“This is an old theory, Babylon’s conspicuous consumption. Sometimes, people want to purchase unnecessary things because of extensive advertising,” he said.
Anwar said the government needs to monitor advertisements, ensure product quality, and strengthen consumer education so people buy what they need and do not spend more than they earn. — Bernama
647d64725e4c646c: SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said his country should expand its ability to launch nuclear weapons from different platforms, state media reported Thursday, stressing that its nuclear capabilities were now a "reality".

Kim made the remarks during an inspection of a nuclear weapons research facility on Wednesday at an unspecified location, following repeated declarations that Pyongyang will not abandon its nuclear weapons.

"The nuclear weapons manufacturing sector should pay attention to utilising the tactical nukes of different missions in multiple domains", the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) quoted him as saying, without elaborating.
It was "an important and urgent task raised from a tactical nukes' military value in modern warfare and from the inevitable reality facing the border with the most dangerous enemy state", he added.
Photos released by KCNA show Kim - flanked by two officials -- looking at rows of what appear to be nuclear warheads, with parts of the objects blurred and some featuring red-painted nose cones.
Another image showed Kim inspecting a series of partially blurred metallic cylindrical devices mounted on wheeled stands.
Reiterating his country's commitment to nuclear weapons, Kim described its nuclear policy as "a core item for guaranteeing the sovereignty of the Republic enshrined in the supreme law of the state".
"No one has the right to force us to go against our Constitution or the right to attempt to amend it," he added.
"Our nuclear capability has now become a reality."

Kim also accused Washington of seeking to replicate its Aukus security pact in Northeast Asia by encouraging its regional allies to acquire nuclear-powered submarines, in an apparent rebuke of Seoul's efforts to acquire such vessels.
Pyongyang enshrined its nuclear weapons policy in its constitution in 2023, a year after adopting a law declaring its status as a nuclear weapons state irreversible.
Kim's message underscores a fundamental shift in the North's approach to nuclear talks with Washington, Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University's Institute for Far Eastern Studies, told AFP.

"It effectively marks the formal abandonment of Pyongyang's previous approach of putting its nuclear arsenal on the negotiating table in exchange for diplomatic recognition or sanctions relief from the US," he said.

"It amounts to the North's declaration that even if Pyongyang and Washington return to the negotiating table, complete, verifiable and irreversible denuclearisation will be off the agenda, with talks limited to managing mutual nuclear threats and arms control," he added.
US president Donald Trump, who met Kim three times during his first term in an effort to curb the North's nuclear programme, said in August that Pyongyang had 57 "very powerful" nuclear weapons.
Seoul estimates that the North possesses between 80 and 120 nuclear weapons.

Trump has repeatedly expressed his willingness to meet Kim for a fourth time, with nuclear negotiations between Washington and Pyongyang having stalled since their 2019 summit in Hanoi ended without a deal.
8adbf6fe2aac820e: KAHERAH: Sekurang-kurangnya 30 maut selepas sebuah lori tangki terbalik dan tebakar di lebuh raya sibuk di Kaherah pada Rabu.

Rakaman AFP menunjukkan bola api besar serta kepulan asap hitam tebal menjulang tinggi di kawasan kejiranan Al-Waraq, Kaherah yang padat dengan penduduk itu, sementara pemandu membunyikan hon dan bertempiaran melarikan diri.
Bangunan di sekitar terselamat daripada kebakaran itu.

Media kerajaan melaporkan sebuah lori membawa muatan bahan api terbalik di jalan lingkaran Kaherah – lebuh raya sibuk yang menghubungkan pelbagai bahagian ibu kota itu – lalu terbakar dan menyebabkan kenderaan berhampiran turut dijilat api.
Kementerian Kesihatan memaklumkan 39 ambulans dikerahkan ke lokasi nahas, dengan 15 mangsa cedera dibawa ke hospital.
“Keadaan di lokasi sangat mengerikan," kata Abdel Rahman Khalil kepada AFP, sambil menambah beliau tiba sejurus nahas berlaku dan melihat lori tangki terbalik itu sedang terbakar.
Pendakwa raya Mesir berkata siasatan telah dimulakan dan ujian DNA sedang dijalankan bagi mengenal pasti mangsa rentung.
Orang ramai dan pasukan perkhidmatan kecemasan berkumpul di lokasi nahas, sementara sebuah jentolak mengalihkan bangkai kereta hangus.
3a93b53fedeb1122: RIYADH: Explosions echoed above Riyadh as Saudi armed forces reported on Thursday downing missiles and drones launched by Yemen's Houthis, just a day after the Iran-backed group claimed strikes on the capital.

Months into Saudi Arabia's renewed war with the Houthis, the kingdom has struggled to shield even its most sensitive infrastructure from attacks, with the fighters striking strategic facilities across the nation and prominent skyscrapers in the heart of Riyadh.

An explosion was heard around midnight (2100 GMT) in Saudi capital Riyadh, according to an AFP journalist and residents, after authorities issued an alert warning of a "hostile aerial threat", which was lifted shortly after.
Residents in northern and eastern Riyadh confirmed hearing the blast, with one saying their house windows "shook violently".

Saudi forces said air defences destroyed two ballistic missiles launched toward the capital by the Houthis, as well as a cruise missile in the western part of the country and a drone near Jeddah's port.
Turki al-Malki, the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition battling the Houthis, said no civilian injuries resulted from the debris of the intercepted drone.
The Houthis said Wednesday they had targeted the Saudi ports of Jeddah and Jazan in response to Saudi strikes on a Yemeni port controlled by the Iran-backed group.
The fighters had also claimed responsibility for attacks a day earlier on the Saudi capital that struck the tallest tower in its financial district, wounding 11.
In recent weeks the group has launched a barrage at Saudi targets including the financial district, airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.

The Saudi coalition has in turn been striking Houthi-held areas of Yemen in support of the internationally recognised government, which has been battling the Houthis for territory since a civil war reignited in July.
Port strikes
"We targeted operational capabilities at the port of Hodeida," the coalition posted to X on Wednesday, having earlier warned civilians to evacuate.
Hodeida is under Houthi control and is a key entry point for goods into Yemeni territory held by the group.

Houthi media outlet Almasirah confirmed on Wednesday morning Hodeida had been targeted and also reported new strikes later in the day, but did not provide details. No casualties or injuries were mentioned.
Almasirah added that Saudi forces had also attacked the area's international airport.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree early on Wednesday threatened to retaliate against Red Sea ports in Saudi Arabia if the coalition went ahead with strikes on Hodeida.
"The port of Jeddah, along with all other Saudi enemy ports along the Red Sea coast, will become targets for our forces should the enemy carry out its threats," he posted on Telegram.
Symbolic target

On the ground in Yemen, the Houthis were pressing their advance against government forces, forcing them to retreat. Houthi fighters are positioned just 60km (37 miles) from Aden, the government's main stronghold in the south.
A Yemeni military spokesman said this week that they were preparing Aden's defences for a potential attack.

On Wednesday, the Houthis claimed responsibility for the strike a day earlier on the Saudi capital's tallest skyscraper, also saying they struck the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom's oil-rich east.
On the Riyadh attack, Houthi spokesman Saree said it had been carried out in three phases, with the strikes hitting their targets "accurately".

The assault on the capital struck its PIF tower, which houses the Saudi sovereign wealth fund. The building had already been targeted last Thursday and is one of several high-profile sites hit since fighting resumed in the summer.
Attacks on the PIF building are symbolic, as the fund is driving efforts to diversify the oil-reliant Saudi economy – a project that has been complicated by the Middle East war and Houthi strikes.
Qatar and Pakistan, who have been acting as mediators in efforts to end the wider regional war between Iran and the United States, both "strongly" condemned the attack on the building.
058893670f2fd19f: PETALING JAYA: When Greg Focker (Ben Stiller) met his future father-in-law in “Meet the Parents”, even a polite conversation with Jack Byrnes (Robert De Niro) felt like an interrogation.

After a welcome like that, you'd think Greg would know better than to put someone else through the same ordeal. But then his son brings home a girlfriend he wants to marry - and suddenly Greg is a lot more like his father-in-law than he would care to admit.
That role reversal sets up “Focker In-Law”, the fourth instalment in the “Meet the Parents” franchise.

Greg and Pam (Teri Polo) are parents to grown-up twins. Their son Henry (Skyler Gisondo) arrives for Jack’s 80th birthday with girlfriend Olivia (Ariana Grande), to whom he plans to propose. His sister Samantha (Beanie Feldstein) also turns up with her boyfriend, Eduardo (Eduardo Franco), who is eager to earn a place in Jack's "Circle of Trust".

It doesn't take long for Olivia, a life coach and former FBI hostage negotiator, to fit in: she and Jack, an ex-CIA operative, hit it off almost immediately. Greg can only watch as she effortlessly wins the approval he had to work so hard to earn.
When Greg learns that Henry plans to propose, he takes it upon himself to prove Olivia is wrong for his son, turning a family gathering into a comedy of increasingly bad decisions.

Much of the fun comes from watching Greg try to rattle someone trained to remain calm under pressure. Grande holds her own alongside Stiller and De Niro, and her comic timing is especially sharp when Greg is at his most flustered. Sometimes, all she has to do is keep a straight face and let him talk!

Stiller slips easily back into the role of Greg, a man whose best intentions somehow make everything worse. The movie throws him into an awkward situation almost immediately, although a little more time to let the tension build might have made the moment funnier.
There's no denying the storyline is predictable, but perhaps that is part of the charm of the franchise: once Greg decides to meddle, you can see where his efforts are headed.
Remember back when Jack was so stern, and Greg so desperate to impress him, that every attempt to win his future father-in-law over only made things worse?

Sadly, there is less of that delicious awkwardness between Greg and the confident Olivia this time around. And even when Greg and Jack fall back into their familiar sparring, it doesn't feel as tense or funny as it used to.

Still, the family dynamics are easy to follow. Longtime fans will also spot a few familiar faces and props - from Pam’s former flame Kevin (Owen Wilson) to Jack’s trusty lie detector - while newbies will have no problem getting acquainted with the Byrnes-Fockers.

Even Mr Jinx the cat makes an appearance - Jack had the late family pet preserved by a taxidermist, so there he sits, still presiding over the household from the top of a cabinet. Of course Jack would give him the best seat in the house!
The Byrnes' German Shepherd, Lazarus, carries on the tradition of making life difficult for Greg, although a few more scenes with the dog might have pushed the chaos, and the comedy, even further.

The film could also have made better use of some of its returning characters. Blythe Danner as Jack's wife, Dina, remains a calming presence amidst the family squabbles, but is given relatively little to do.

And while Greg’s parents, Bernie and Roz, do not appear, their absence is felt. Dustin Hoffman and Barbra Streisand brought such free-spirited energy to the earlier movies that it is hard not to wonder what they would have made of Greg's slow evolution into Jack.

Still, there are enough laughs to make “Focker In-Law” a fun, easy watch. The best ones come when Greg tries to channel his inner Jack - and discovers he is just as capable of making a mess from the other side of the interrogation.
As of press time, ‘Focker In-Law’ is screening in cinemas nationwide.
26a23f5bbfd78fef: PETALING JAYA: Ketidakpuasan hati terhadap Pakatan Harapan (PH) tidak semestinya bermaksud pengundi lebih meyakini Barisan Nasional (BN), kata penganalisis, sambil menggesa parti-parti politik membuktikan perubahan melalui tindakan.

Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri dari Global Asia Consulting berkata pengundi sememangnya sedar akan jurang antara prinsip yang diperjuangkan sesebuah parti ketika menjadi pembangkang berbanding keputusan yang dibuat apabila ia memegang kuasa.
"Pengundi tidak semestinya menjadi penyokong Perikatan Nasional atau BN. Mereka mungkin sebaliknya sedang hilang keyakinan terhadap PH," katanya kepada FMT.
Beliau berkata pengundi menolak BN khususnya Umno kerana menginginkan reformasi, integriti dan keadilan, bukannya semata-mata kerana menggemari PH.

Penilaian ini menyusuli PRN Melaka, yang menyaksikan BN dan PN pimpinan PAS memenangi 25 kerusi dengan bertanding sebagai satu pakatan, manakala PH hanya memperoleh empat kerusi yang kesemuanya dimenangi DAP.
Zaharuddin berkata kekurangan jumlah kerusi PH di Dewan Rakyat menyukarkan pelaksanaan reformasi, namun mengusahakan perubahan dan kebertanggungjawaban tetap perkara penting.

PH dan sekutunya ketika itu, Muda, memenangi 82 kerusi pada PRU 2022, kurang daripada 112 kerusi yang diperlukan untuk membentuk kerajaan dengan majoriti mudah. Kerajaan perpaduan akhirnya terbentuk dengan kerjasama BN dan gabungan lain.

Zaharuddin berkata kerjasama itu perlu bagi memastikan kestabilan politik, namun ia tidak menjawab kebimbangan dalam kalangan penyokong PH mengenai kerjasama dengan parti yang sekian lama dikritik atas isu integriti.
Beliau juga berkata pertimbangan politik tidak seharusnya mempengaruhi kes melibatkan pemimpin politik daripada pentadbiran terdahulu.
Zaharuddin menambah pengundi sukar menerima penjelasan yang pernah ditolak oleh parti-parti berkenaan ketika menjadi pembangkang, walaupun mereka mungkin memahami kekangan kewangan dan pentadbiran.
Perjuangan lalu tak lagi memikat pengundi muda
Azmi Hassan dari Akademi Nusantara berkata Umno tidak lagi boleh bergantung kepada peranannya dalam memperjuangkan kemerdekaan untuk memenangi hati pengundi muda.

Azmi berkata agenda reformasi PH mesti menunjukkan manfaat yang nyata kepada pengundi.
